Explore five moments in a growing business—and the LetBuyy tools you can use at each one. 01 Launch Store Launch 02 First Order Sell 03 Scale Operations Operate 04 Build Brand Retain 05 Enterprise Expand Storefronts + Themes Make it yours. Then open the doors. Turn your products into a storefront that feels like your business. Start with the essentials and publish when you are ready. Shape your storefront Choose a theme, adjust your branding and preview it on different screens. Prepare your catalogue Add product photos, prices, sizes and available stock. Make it easy to find Use your LetBuyy address or connect an eligible custom domain. Orders + Payments Your first sale. A clear next step. When a customer buys, bring the order, payment and delivery details together. Follow the work from purchase to a prepared parcel. Review the purchase See what was ordered, who bought it and where it needs to go. Follow the payment Check whether the order is paid, pending or cash on delivery. Prepare the parcel Pack the items, add shipment details and follow delivery progress. Inventory + Orders More orders. A more organised day. Keep the stockroom and the order list working together. Know what is available, what needs attention and what is ready to leave. Know your stock Review available quantities for each product and variant. Plan a restock Check stock history and prepare incoming inventory or purchase orders. Keep fulfilment moving Follow pending orders, shipment updates and returns in your workspace. Customers + Analytics Give a first-time buyer a reason to return. Get to know your customers and plan your next collection with better context. Build the relationship beyond one transaction. Understand your customers Find customer profiles, purchase history and useful segments. Share the next collection Prepare email campaigns for customers who have subscribed. Learn from your sales Review product performance and revenue before planning your next move. B2B + AI + Analytics A wider business. A connected workspace. As the business becomes more complex, bring wholesale work, AI assistance and reporting into the same operating picture. Organise wholesale work Manage business buyers and bulk-order workflows alongside your retail operations. Work with AI assistance Prepare supported content drafts and review suggestions before acting. Keep the wider view Use your commerce reports to understand the business across its activities. Previous 01 / 05 Next stage Tools depend on your plan and setup. Payments, shipping and live email delivery require the relevant provider connections. How LetBuyy works Build your store. Run the business behind it. LetBuyy brings your online shop, orders and customer tools into one workspace. Here’s how they help you, from opening day to your next collection. 01 Make it yours Your products. Your own online store. Give your business a home online, with your branding and a storefront that works on phones, tablets and computers. Choose a theme and make it your own. Add product photos, prices, sizes and stock. Preview your shop, connect your domain and publish. Explore storefront themes 02 Start selling From a customer’s basket to a packed order. Share your store link. Let customers browse and buy, then manage each order from your merchant workspace. Offer the payment methods you have enabled. See purchases, payment status and stock together. Prepare shipments, add tracking and handle returns. See how order fulfilment works 03 Keep them coming back Turn a first purchase into a relationship. Understand who buys from you, share your next collection and use your sales reports to decide what to do next. Find customer profiles and purchase history. Prepare email campaigns for subscribed customers. Review orders and revenue to plan your next move. Read the email marketing guide Payment, shipping and email options depend on your plan, account setup and connected providers. An everyday example One T-shirt sold. The next steps, together. A customer buys a navy T-shirt from your store. Follow the work that comes next, with the order details in one place. 01 See the order The products, buyer and delivery details are together. 02 Check the payment Know whether it is paid, pending or cash on delivery. 03 Keep stock accurate Review available quantities before the next sale. 04 Prepare delivery Pack the order and keep shipment progress up to date. What does that mean for your day? Start with the job you need to do. An order comes in + Open the order to see the items, customer, payment and delivery details. Follow its progress from preparation through delivery. A payment needs checking + Look at the order’s payment status and transaction details. An online payment and a cash-on-delivery order can be followed separately. A customer needs a refund + Review the order and refund details in your workspace. Follow the refund status through your connected payment provider rather than assuming it has completed. A product is running low + Check quantities for each product and variant, review stock history and prepare a restock or purchase order. You have a new collection to share + Create an email campaign, choose subscribed customers or a customer segment, preview the audience and review the message before sending. Live email delivery requires email setup. You want to understand your earnings + Review sales, payments, refunds and available settlement information. Payment-provider processing and settlement timing are separate from an order being placed. Pricing Simple, transparent pricing Launch and Growth plans are live now. Scale and Commerce OS are coming soon. 0% transaction and platform fees — forever. Frequently Asked Questions Everything you need to know before launching Answers to the most common questions about pricing, migration, payments, data ownership, and how LetBuyy compares to traditional commerce platforms. Built for modern commerce No transaction commissions Indian payment ecosystem Custom domains supported Migration assistance available AI-native commerce platform AI capabilities 50+ Monitoring 24/7 Data ownership 100% Commission 0% What is LetBuyy? LetBuyy is an AI-native Commerce Operating System that helps businesses manage storefronts, products, inventory, orders, payments, customers, analytics, and operations from one platform. Unlike traditional store builders, LetBuyy is designed to run the entire commerce business, not just the online store. How is LetBuyy different from Shopify? Can I use my own custom domain? Which payment methods does LetBuyy support? Can I migrate from Shopify, WooCommerce, or another platform? Is LetBuyy suitable for growing businesses? Do you charge transaction commissions? What happens after my free trial ends? Who owns my store data? LetBuyy Ecosystem One platform. Many powerful surfaces. Everything merchants, developers, operators, and partners need to run commerce from one connected ecosystem. 12+ Platform Surfaces 1 Unified Identity 100% Commerce Engine AI Native Foundation Core Platform Merchant Control Plane The operating system behind every LetBuyy store. pages.text: Changelog — LetBuyy | LetBuyy Resources Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Resources All Ecommerce Growth Payments Operations AI Commerce Developers Changelog Commerce updates Resources A PRODUCT IN PROGRESS Changelog Every update. A little more possibility. Every release, newest first. LetBuyy is in private beta — expect this list to move quickly. Explore the updates Follow via RSS Thoughtful changes, recorded along the way. Concept illustration. Releases so far 9 Latest version v 1.9.0 Latest release 22 Jul 2026 THE RELEASE JOURNAL What changed. New features, thoughtful improvements and fixes along the way. All updates 9 New features 6 Fixes 1 Security 1 Improvements 1 9 releases · Newest first v 1.9.0 22 Jul 2026 New features Latest release PRODUCT UPDATE Theme marketplace opens to partner submissions Added Design partners can now submit themes for review from the developer portal Added Every submission runs an automated safety check before it reaches a live store Improved Theme previews now render your own products instead of placeholder samples Improved Switching themes keeps your existing section settings where the layouts match v 1.8.1 9 Jul 2026 Fixes PRODUCT UPDATE Checkout and GST invoice fixes Fixed Inter-state orders now show IGST correctly instead of splitting into CGST and SGST Fixed Double-tapping Place Order on a slow connection no longer creates a duplicate order Fixed COD confirmation messages now send reliably to numbers saved with a +91 prefix Improved The GST invoice PDF is now attached to the order confirmation email automatically v 1.8.0 24 Jun 2026 New features PRODUCT UPDATE Gift cards and store credit Added Issue gift cards with a fixed value and an optional expiry date Added Buyers can apply a gift card at checkout alongside a coupon Added Refunds can be returned as store credit instead of to the original payment method Improved Gift card balances now appear on the customer profile with full redemption history v 1.7.0 5 Jun 2026 New features PRODUCT UPDATE WhatsApp order updates Added Send order confirmation, shipping and delivery updates over WhatsApp Added Message templates in English and Hindi, editable per store Improved COD orders can now ask for a WhatsApp confirmation before they enter fulfilment v 1.6.2 21 May 2026 Security PRODUCT UPDATE Account and payment hardening Improved Payment provider callbacks are now verified with a timing-safe signature check Improved Store sign-in is rate limited to five attempts every fifteen minutes Improved Refunds and payouts now require a second confirmation step Fixed Signing out now ends the session on every device, not just the current one v 1.6.0 6 May 2026 New features PRODUCT UPDATE Multi-location inventory (beta) Added Hold stock across more than one warehouse or shop Added pages.text: Terms of Service Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Agreements / Terms Terms of Service The agreement between you and LetBuyy for using the platform. Applies to Merchants Clauses 11 Reading time 5 min Revised 3 August 2026 These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 11 Contents 01 What this agreement covers 02 Who sells to your customers 03 Your account 04 Your content and data 05 What you may sell 06 Fees 07 Availability and changes 08 Suspension and termination 09 Liability 10 Governing law and disputes 11 Changes to these terms In short LetBuyy gives you software to run an online store. You remain the seller — your customers buy from you, not from us. You keep ownership of your products, content, customer list, and data. We do not sell your catalogue or compete with you. We charge no commission on your sales. Payment providers charge their own fees, which we do not control or receive. You are responsible for what you sell, what you tell customers, and the taxes you owe. We are responsible for the platform working. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 What this agreement covers These terms apply when you create a LetBuyy account, open a store, or use any part of the platform — the merchant dashboard, storefronts on a letbuyy.com subdomain or your own domain, the mobile merchant app, themes, apps, and the APIs. If you use LetBuyy on behalf of a company, you confirm you are authorised to bind that company, and "you" means the company. Note Separate documents govern payouts, refunds, data processing, and marketplace publishing. Where a specialised document conflicts with these terms, the specialised one governs that subject. 02 Who sells to your customers LetBuyy is a technology provider. When a shopper buys from a store built on LetBuyy, the contract of sale is between that shopper and you. We are not a party to it, do not take title to your goods, and do not act as your agent. This means the obligations that attach to a seller attach to you: describing goods accurately, honouring the delivery timelines you publish, processing returns under your stated policy, issuing tax invoices, and answering your customers. We may display your store name, logo, or storefront in examples of platform capability. Tell us to stop and we will. 03 Your account You need an account to open a store. Keep your credentials confidential — activity under your account is treated as yours. Tell us immediately if you believe someone else has access. Sensitive actions such as issuing refunds and changing payout destinations require additional verification beyond your password. This is deliberate and cannot be disabled. One person or company may operate multiple stores. Each store is isolated: its data is not readable from another store, including your own. 04 Your content and data You own your product catalogue, media, storefront content, customer records, and order history. Using LetBuyy does not transfer any of it to us. You grant us the limited licence needed to actually run the service — to store your content, serve it to shoppers, back it up, index it for search within your own store, and transmit it to the providers listed in our sub-processor register. We do not sell your data, do not use your customer list to market to your customers, and do not use your catalogue to build a competing product. 05 What you may sell You are responsible for the legality of everything you list. Some categories are prohibited outright and some are restricted; both are set out in the Acceptable Use Policy, which forms part of this agreement. Payment providers and card networks impose their own category restrictions. A listing that we permit may still be refused by a payment provider, and we cannot override that. 06 Fees LetBuyy charges no commission and no per-transaction platform fee on your sales. Subscription pricing, where it applies, is shown on the pricing page before you subscribe. Payment providers, shipping partners, and any paid apps you install charge their own fees directly. Those are not ours, we do not receive a share of them, and we cannot waive them. Where we owe GST on amounts we charge you, it is stated separately on our invoice. 07 Availability and changes We work to keep the platform available and will give reasonable notice of planned maintenance that affects storefronts. We do not promise uninterrupted service. We may add, change, or remove features. Where a change removes something you depend on, we will give notice proportionate to the disruption and, where practical, a migration path. Some surfaces — the app marketplace, the theme marketplace, and the developer portal — are not open for new publishing. Their status is stated on the relevant pages and in the Marketplace Partner Terms. 08 Suspension and termination You may close your account at any time. Before you do, export what you need — see the Data Processing Addendum for what happens to your data afterwards. We may suspend a store immediately where it is being used for fraud, where it is causing harm to shoppers or to the platform, or where we are legally required to. Otherwise we will raise the problem with you and give you a reasonable chance to fix it first. Suspension does not extinguish money already owed to you. Funds already settled remain yours; funds held against open disputes are handled under the Payouts and Settlements policy. 09 Liability The platform is provided as-is beyond the warranties we cannot exclude by law. We are not liable for your lost profits, lost sales, or lost data, or for the acts of your customers, suppliers, or the payment and shipping providers you choose. Where liability cannot be excluded, our total liability across all claims in any twelve-month period is limited to the fees you paid us in that period. Nothing in this clause limits liability for fraud, wilful misconduct, or anything else that cannot be limited under Indian law. Note Because we charge no commission, the fee cap above may be zero for merchants on a free plan. That is the honest consequence of the pricing model and you should weigh it. 10 Governing law and disputes This agreement is governed by the laws of India. Talk to us first — most disputes resolve faster through the grievance process than through a court, and the Grievance Redressal policy sets out the timelines we hold ourselves to. 11 Changes to these terms We will post a revised version here and update the revision date. For changes that materially reduce your rights or increase your obligations, we will notify account holders by email before the change takes effect. Continuing to use LetBuyy after a change takes effect means you accept the revised terms. If you do not, close your account before that date. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . We do not promise uninterrupted service. We may add, change, or remove features. Where a change removes something you depend on, we will give notice proportionate to the disruption and, where practical, a migration path. Some surfaces — the app marketplace, the theme marketplace, and the developer portal — are not open for new publishing. Their status is stated on the relevant pages and in the Marketplace Partner Terms. 08 Suspension and termination You may close your account at any time. Before you do, export what you need — see the Data Processing Addendum for what happens to your data afterwards. We may suspend a store immediately where it is being used for fraud, where it is causing harm to shoppers or to the platform, or where we are legally required to. Otherwise we will raise the problem with you and give you a reasonable chance to fix it first. Suspension does not extinguish money already owed to you. Funds already settled remain yours; funds held against open disputes are handled under the Payouts and Settlements policy. 09 Liability The platform is provided as-is beyond the warranties we cannot exclude by law. We are not liable for your lost profits, lost sales, or lost data, or for the acts of your customers, suppliers, or the payment and shipping providers you choose. Where liability cannot be excluded, our total liability across all claims in any twelve-month period is limited to the fees you paid us in that period. Nothing in this clause limits liability for fraud, wilful misconduct, or anything else that cannot be limited under Indian law. Note Because we charge no commission, the fee cap above may be zero for merchants on a free plan. That is the honest consequence of the pricing model and you should weigh it. 10 Governing law and disputes This agreement is governed by the laws of India. Talk to us first — most disputes resolve faster through the grievance process than through a court, and the Grievance Redressal policy sets out the timelines we hold ourselves to. 11 Changes to these terms We will post a revised version here and update the revision date. For changes that materially reduce your rights or increase your obligations, we will notify account holders by email before the change takes effect. Continuing to use LetBuyy after a change takes effect means you accept the revised terms. If you do not, close your account before that date. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . Next Acceptable Use Policy

pages.text: Acceptable Use Policy Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Agreements / Acceptable use Acceptable Use Policy What may and may not be sold or done on LetBuyy. Applies to Merchants Clauses 5 Reading time 3 min Revised 3 August 2026 These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 5 Contents 01 Prohibited — never permitted 02 Restricted — permitted with the right licence 03 How you must behave 04 Technical limits 05 How we enforce this In short Some things cannot be sold on LetBuyy at all. Others need a licence or extra checks before you can list them. These limits come from three places: Indian law, payment provider rules, and our own judgement about shopper harm. If you are unsure whether your category is allowed, ask before you build. We would rather answer early than suspend a working store. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 Prohibited — never permitted Listing any of the following will result in removal, and repeated or deliberate listing in account termination. Narcotics, psychotropic substances, and drug paraphernalia Weapons, ammunition, explosives, and their components Wildlife products, protected species, and items banned under the Wildlife Protection Act Human organs, tissue, and bodily fluids Counterfeit goods and anything infringing another party's trademark or copyright Sexually explicit material and any material involving minors Stolen goods, and tools whose primary purpose is theft or unauthorised access Forged documents, identity documents, and government credentials Prescription medicines sold without the prescription and licence the law requires Multi-level marketing schemes, chain schemes, and money-circulation schemes Unlicensed financial products, lending, or investment schemes Betting, gambling, and lottery services without the applicable state licence Cryptocurrency exchange or custody services 02 Restricted — permitted with the right licence These categories are legitimate but regulated. You may sell them once you hold the licence the law requires and have told us, and a payment provider may still decline the category independently. Food, beverages, and supplements — FSSAI registration or licence Cosmetics and personal care — CDSCO registration where applicable Alcohol — the applicable state excise licence, where online sale is permitted at all Tobacco and nicotine products, subject to COTPA restrictions Medical devices and diagnostic products Ayurvedic, Siddha, Unani, and homoeopathic preparations — AYUSH licensing Precious metals, gemstones, and jewellery — hallmarking obligations Pesticides, agricultural chemicals, and seeds Second-hand and refurbished electronics, which must be described as such Digital goods and subscriptions, which must state renewal terms before purchase 03 How you must behave Beyond what you sell, how you operate matters. You must not: Describe goods inaccurately, or hide charges until checkout Publish fake reviews, fake scarcity, or fake discount reference prices Collect payment for goods you have no intention or ability to deliver Use a storefront primarily to test stolen payment credentials Send unsolicited marketing to people who did not consent Impersonate another business, or imply a LetBuyy endorsement you do not have Publish content that harasses, defames, or incites violence against any person or group 04 Technical limits The platform is shared infrastructure. You must not attempt to reach another store's data, probe for vulnerabilities outside a disclosure programme, run automated traffic that degrades service for others, or circumvent rate limits and bot protection. Themes and apps must not exfiltrate shopper data, inject undisclosed tracking, or load code that changes behaviour after review. 05 How we enforce this Most breaches get a notice and a window to fix. Fraud, shopper harm, and legal compulsion get immediate action, because waiting causes more damage than acting. Where we remove a listing or suspend a store, we tell you what triggered it and what would resolve it, unless a law forbids us from saying. You can escalate any enforcement decision through the grievance process. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . Previous Terms of Service Next Developer & API Terms LetBuyy footer LetBuyy What is LetBuyy? pages.text: Developer & API Terms Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Agreements / API terms Developer & API Terms Rules for building against the LetBuyy APIs, webhooks, and themes. Applies to Developers Clauses 7 Reading time 3 min Revised 3 August 2026 These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 7 Contents 01 Getting access 02 Credentials 03 Store isolation 04 Webhooks 05 Rate limits and fair use 06 Merchant and shopper data 07 Themes In short You may build integrations against LetBuyy for a merchant who has authorised you. API credentials are tied to a specific store. Using one to reach a different store is a breach, not a bug to exploit. Webhooks are signed. Verify the signature before you trust the payload — an unverified webhook endpoint is an open door. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 Getting access API access is granted per store, by the merchant who owns that store. Credentials carry the scopes the merchant approved and nothing more. The developer portal is currently closed to new public app registrations. Existing integrations continue to work; new ones are onboarded case by case. 02 Credentials Treat API keys and secrets as you would a password. Do not commit them, do not ship them in client-side code, and do not share them between merchants. If a credential leaks, rotate it immediately and tell us. We would rather hear it from you. We may revoke a credential without notice if we see it being used from an unexpected pattern that suggests compromise. 03 Store isolation Every record on LetBuyy belongs to exactly one store, and that boundary is enforced in the database, not just in application code. Deliberately probing for cross-store access is a breach of these terms and, depending on what you reach, an offence under the Information Technology Act. If you find a way across that boundary, report it rather than using it. We will not pursue a good-faith reporter who stops at proof and tells us promptly. 04 Webhooks Webhook payloads are signed with a shared secret. Verify the signature on every delivery using a constant-time comparison before acting on the contents. Deliveries may arrive more than once. Make your handler idempotent — key on the event id, not on the fact that a request arrived. Endpoints that fail repeatedly are backed off and eventually disabled. Delivery records are retained for 90 days, which is your window to reconcile a gap. Note An endpoint that skips signature verification will accept anything anyone sends it. This is the single most common integration vulnerability we see. 05 Rate limits and fair use The APIs are rate limited. Handle a 429 by backing off, not by retrying immediately from more workers. Do not poll for changes you could receive as a webhook. Polling at high frequency across many stores is the fastest way to get throttled. 06 Merchant and shopper data Data you reach through the API belongs to the merchant, and often describes their customers. You may use it only to provide the function the merchant installed you for. You may not build a profile of shoppers across merchants, sell derived data, or retain data after the merchant uninstalls you beyond what law requires. If you process personal data on a merchant's behalf, you are their processor and the obligations in the Data Processing Addendum apply to you too. 07 Themes Theme templates are rendered through a sanitiser that escapes output and blocks a fixed list of dangerous constructs. Do not attempt to defeat it. A theme must not load third-party scripts that were not disclosed at review, collect shopper input beyond what the storefront needs, or alter checkout behaviour. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . Make your handler idempotent — key on the event id, not on the fact that a request arrived. Endpoints that fail repeatedly are backed off and eventually disabled. Delivery records are retained for 90 days, which is your window to reconcile a gap. Note An endpoint that skips signature verification will accept anything anyone sends it. This is the single most common integration vulnerability we see. 05 Rate limits and fair use The APIs are rate limited. Handle a 429 by backing off, not by retrying immediately from more workers. Do not poll for changes you could receive as a webhook. Polling at high frequency across many stores is the fastest way to get throttled. 06 Merchant and shopper data Data you reach through the API belongs to the merchant, and often describes their customers. You may use it only to provide the function the merchant installed you for. You may not build a profile of shoppers across merchants, sell derived data, or retain data after the merchant uninstalls you beyond what law requires. If you process personal data on a merchant's behalf, you are their processor and the obligations in the Data Processing Addendum apply to you too. 07 Themes Theme templates are rendered through a sanitiser that escapes output and blocks a fixed list of dangerous constructs. Applies to Developers Clauses 6 Reading time 2 min Revised 3 August 2026 These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 6 Contents 01 Current marketplace status 02 Review and approval 03 Permissions 04 Support and lifecycle 05 Commercial terms 06 Removal In short These terms apply if you publish an app or theme that other merchants install. The app and theme marketplaces are currently closed to new public submissions. Existing listings remain governed by this document. You are responsible for your listing working, for supporting it, and for what it does with merchant and shopper data. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 Current marketplace status The app marketplace, theme marketplace, and developer portal are frozen for new public submissions while the platform completes its launch scope. This is a product state, not a permanent decision. Listings already published continue to operate and are governed by these terms. 02 Review and approval Submissions are reviewed before they reach merchants. Review covers functionality, the permissions requested, data handling, and whether the listing describes what it actually does. Approval is not an endorsement and does not transfer responsibility for your code to us. We may re-review a listing at any time, particularly after an update, and may unlist it if it no longer matches what was approved. 03 Permissions Request the narrowest scopes your listing actually needs. A listing that requests broad access without a stated reason will not pass review. If an update needs a wider scope, the merchant must be asked again. Silently widening access is grounds for removal. 04 Support and lifecycle You support your own listing. Publish a working contact route and respond to merchants within a reasonable time. If you discontinue a listing, give installed merchants notice and a way to export any data your listing holds. Vanishing without notice is a breach. 05 Commercial terms Where a listing is paid, the revenue share and settlement schedule are set out in your partner agreement rather than here, because they vary by listing type. You are responsible for the tax treatment of your own earnings, including GST registration where your turnover requires it. 06 Removal We may remove a listing that breaks, that misrepresents itself, that mishandles data, or that breaches the Acceptable Use Policy. Where removal is not urgent, we will tell you first and give you a chance to fix the problem. Where shopper data is at risk, we act first and explain after. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . pages.text: Billing, Plans & Taxes Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Money & orders / Billing Billing, Plans & Taxes What LetBuyy charges you, when, and how tax is handled. Applies to Merchants Clauses 6 Reading time 2 min Revised 3 August 2026 These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 6 Contents 01 No commission 02 Fees we do not control 03 Subscription billing 04 GST on what we charge you 05 GST on what you sell 06 Records In short LetBuyy takes no commission on your sales and charges no per-transaction platform fee. Where a plan carries a subscription price, it is shown on the pricing page before you subscribe and billed in advance. Payment providers, shipping partners, and paid apps bill you separately. Those fees are theirs, not ours. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 No commission We do not take a percentage of your sales, and we do not add a platform fee to your transactions. Your revenue arrives from your payment provider without a deduction by us. This is a pricing commitment, not an introductory offer. If it ever changes, existing merchants get notice before the change applies to them. 02 Fees we do not control Your payment provider charges a processing fee on each transaction, set by them and visible in their dashboard. Shipping partners charge for shipments. Paid apps charge their own subscription. None of these flow through us and we receive no share of them. We cannot waive, refund, or negotiate them on your behalf. 03 Subscription billing Paid plans are billed in advance for the period you select. The price, currency, and period are shown before you confirm. Plan changes take effect from the next billing period unless the change is an upgrade, which takes effect immediately with a pro-rated charge. If a subscription payment fails, we retry and notify you. Extended non-payment moves the store to a restricted state rather than deleting it — see the Data Processing Addendum for retention. 04 GST on what we charge you Where LetBuyy charges you and GST applies, it is stated separately on our invoice along with our GSTIN. Provide your GSTIN in your account settings if you want it on our invoices. We cannot reissue a past invoice to add a GSTIN that was not on file when it was raised. 05 GST on what you sell Tax on your sales is yours to charge, collect, and remit. The platform computes GST server-side from the rates and place-of-supply rules configured for your store, and issues an invoice against each order. Invoices are immutable once issued. A correction is made by a credit note against the original, never by editing it — this is both a legal requirement and how the ledger is built. Configuring the wrong HSN code or rate produces a wrong invoice. The computation is ours; the configuration is yours. Note We provide tax computation, not tax advice. Whether you must register for GST, and at what rate you must charge, is a question for your accountant. 06 Records Invoices, orders, and the payment ledger are retained for the period Indian tax and company law requires, which is longer than the retention period for ordinary account data. You can export your own records at any time from the dashboard. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. pages.text: Payouts & Settlements Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Money & orders / Payouts Payouts & Settlements How money from your sales reaches your bank account. Applies to Merchants Clauses 7 Reading time 3 min Revised 3 August 2026 These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 7 Contents 01 Where the money actually sits 02 Settlement timing 03 Cash on delivery 04 Holds and reserves 05 Chargebacks and disputes 06 Changing your payout destination 07 If you close your store In short Money from card, UPI, and netbanking orders is collected by your payment provider and settled to your bank account on their schedule. LetBuyy does not hold your money. We record what is owed; the provider moves it. Cash-on-delivery money reaches you through your courier, not through the payment provider or us. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 Where the money actually sits For online payments, funds move from the shopper to your payment provider, and from the provider to your bank account. They do not pass through a LetBuyy account. We maintain the ledger — what was charged, captured, refunded, and owed — and reconcile it against the provider. The ledger is the record; the provider is the custodian. This matters if something goes wrong: a settlement that has not arrived is a question for your provider, and we can show you exactly what the ledger says to support that conversation. 02 Settlement timing Your settlement cycle is set by your payment provider and shown in their dashboard. Typical cycles for Indian merchants run from same-day to T+3 business days, and new accounts often start on a longer cycle. Bank holidays and weekends shift settlement. A payment captured on a Friday evening commonly settles the following week. 03 Cash on delivery For COD orders, your courier collects cash from the shopper and remits it to you under your agreement with them, on their own cycle. No payment provider is involved. The platform records a COD order as pending until you confirm collection, so your ledger reflects money actually received rather than money expected. COD remittance disputes are between you and your courier. We can evidence what was ordered and marked delivered. 04 Holds and reserves Payment providers may hold a rolling reserve against a merchant account, or hold specific funds pending a chargeback. That decision is theirs and is governed by your agreement with them. Where we are told funds are held, we reflect it in your dashboard so the number you see matches the number you will receive. 05 Chargebacks and disputes When a shopper disputes a card payment, the provider debits the amount pending resolution and asks for evidence. The window is short — often seven days. You respond to the dispute; we supply the order, delivery, and communication records to help you do it. We cannot represent you to the network. Repeated chargebacks put your payment account at risk with the provider, independently of anything we do. 06 Changing your payout destination Changing the bank account money settles to requires step-up verification beyond your password. This cannot be turned off. This is the single most attractive target on any commerce account. The friction is intentional. Note We will never email or call you asking to confirm bank details. If someone does, it is not us — report it through the grievance process. 07 If you close your store Closing a LetBuyy store does not close your payment provider account, and does not stop settlements already in flight. Settle open orders and let the dispute window pass before closing either. Money owed to you does not disappear because the storefront is gone. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . pages.text: Refunds & Cancellations Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Money & orders / Refunds Refunds & Cancellations How refunds work on LetBuyy — and who decides them. Applies to Everyone Clauses 7 Reading time 3 min Revised 3 August 2026 These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 7 Contents 01 If you bought from a store on LetBuyy 02 How a refund travels 03 Refunds on cash-on-delivery orders 04 Partial refunds and gift cards 05 For merchants: your obligations 06 For merchants: refund controls 07 Refunds of LetBuyy subscription fees In short If you bought something from a store built on LetBuyy, your refund is decided by that store under its own policy — not by us. Once a merchant issues a refund, the money returns by the route it was paid, and the timing is set by your bank. This page also covers refunds of what LetBuyy charges merchants directly. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 If you bought from a store on LetBuyy Your purchase contract is with the store, not with LetBuyy. The store sets its return window, its condition requirements, and who pays return shipping, and publishes them in its own refund policy. Contact the store first — its contact details are in the storefront footer and on your order confirmation. It can see your order and act on it; we cannot act on it for them. If a store will not respond or refuses to honour its own published policy, escalate to us through the grievance process. We can reach the merchant and, where a store is behaving badly, act against it. Note We cannot force a merchant to refund you, and we cannot refund you from our own funds. What we can do is escalate, evidence, and enforce our policies against a store that misbehaves. 02 How a refund travels Refunds return by the original payment route. A card payment goes back to that card; UPI goes back to the paying account. We cannot redirect a refund to a different destination. Once the merchant issues it, the payment provider processes it and the shopper's bank credits it. Typical end-to-end time for Indian banks is five to seven business days, sometimes longer for credit cards where it appears on the next statement. The delay after the merchant acts is bank-side. A merchant showing "refunded" and a bank not yet showing the credit is the normal state for several days. 03 Refunds on cash-on-delivery orders There is no original payment route to reverse, so a COD refund is paid out separately — usually by bank transfer or UPI to details the shopper provides. That makes COD refunds slower and more manual than online-payment refunds, and it makes them a common target for impersonation. A shopper should only ever give refund details to the store they actually bought from. 04 Partial refunds and gift cards A merchant can refund part of an order — a single item, or an amount. The ledger records each movement against the original order, so a partially refunded order stays reconcilable. Where an order was paid partly with a gift card, the gift-card portion is restored to the gift card and the remainder returns to the payment method. The balance is rebuilt from the ledger rather than adjusted directly, so it cannot drift. 05 For merchants: your obligations You must publish a refund policy on your storefront. Payment providers require it before they will onboard you, and consumer law requires you to honour what you publish. State the return window, the condition goods must be in, who pays return shipping, and how long a refund takes. Vague policies generate disputes you will lose. You may not charge a cancellation fee that you do not also bear when you are the one cancelling. 06 For merchants: refund controls Issuing a refund requires step-up verification. Refunds are irreversible once processed and are an obvious target if an account is compromised. Every refund is recorded against the order with the account that authorised it. This is your audit trail in a dispute. 07 Refunds of LetBuyy subscription fees Subscription fees are charged in advance. If you cancel mid-period, your plan runs to the end of the period you paid for and does not renew; we do not pro-rate the unused part. If we charged you in error, tell us and we will correct it — that is a mistake, not a cancellation. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . Previous Payouts & Settlements Next Shipping & Delivery LetBuyy footer LetBuyy What is LetBuyy? pages.text: Shipping & Delivery Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Money & orders / Shipping Shipping & Delivery How delivery works, and where responsibility for it sits. Applies to Everyone Clauses 7 Reading time 2 min Revised 3 August 2026 These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 7 Contents 01 Who ships your order 02 How shipping is calculated 03 Delivery timelines 04 Tracking and delivery confirmation 05 Cash on delivery 06 Lost, damaged, and undelivered 07 For merchants: what you must publish In short Every store on LetBuyy sets its own shipping rates, zones, and delivery timelines. There is no platform-wide shipping policy that overrides them. Shopper-facing delivery obligations belong to the store you bought from. This page explains the mechanism the platform provides and what each side is responsible for. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 Who ships your order The merchant does. LetBuyy provides the software that calculates a rate at checkout and records fulfilment; it does not warehouse goods, pack them, or hand them to a courier. The courier is chosen by the merchant. Delivery performance is a matter between the merchant and that courier. 02 How shipping is calculated Merchants configure shipping rates by zone — commonly by pincode range, state, or weight band. At checkout, the platform resolves the applicable rate for the delivery address and adds it to the order total server-side. The total a shopper is charged is computed on our servers from the merchant's configuration, never from values the browser sends. This is why a shipping amount cannot be altered by tampering with the checkout page. If no rate matches an address, the store cannot deliver there and checkout will say so rather than guessing. 03 Delivery timelines Timelines shown at checkout are the merchant's estimates for their courier and zone. They are estimates, not guarantees, and are affected by weather, festivals, strikes, and regional restrictions. Consumer law requires a seller to deliver within the time stated, or within a reasonable time where none is stated. That obligation is the merchant's. 04 Tracking and delivery confirmation Where the merchant supplies a tracking reference, it appears on the order and in the shopper's confirmation email. Tracking data comes from the courier and is only as current as they make it. A courier marking an order delivered is the courier's record. Where a shopper disputes it, the merchant investigates with the courier. 05 Cash on delivery Not every courier serves every pincode for COD, and many impose an order-value ceiling. A store may therefore offer COD in some places and not others. Where a COD order is refused at the door, the goods return to the merchant and the merchant bears the return freight under their courier agreement. 06 Lost, damaged, and undelivered Risk in the goods passes on delivery. Until then, a lost or damaged parcel is the merchant's problem to resolve with the shopper, whatever they later recover from the courier. Shoppers should raise a damaged delivery with the store promptly and keep the packaging — courier claims usually require it. 07 For merchants: what you must publish Publish your delivery timelines, serviceable areas, shipping charges, and what happens when a delivery fails. Payment providers require a shipping policy for physical goods before onboarding, and consumer law requires the information before purchase. Keep serviceability current. A store that accepts orders it cannot deliver generates refunds, disputes, and eventually payment-provider scrutiny. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . pages.text: Privacy Policy Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Data & privacy / Privacy Privacy Policy What personal data LetBuyy handles, why, and what rights you have. Applies to Everyone Clauses 11 Reading time 5 min Revised 3 August 2026 These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 11 Contents 01 Two different relationships 02 What we collect from merchants 03 What stores collect from shoppers 04 Why we process it 05 Consent 06 Who else sees it 07 How long we keep it 08 Your rights 09 How it is protected 10 Children 11 Changes In short For merchant accounts, LetBuyy decides what data is collected and why — so we answer to you directly for it. For shopper data inside a store, the merchant decides and we process on their instruction. Ask the store first; we will help them answer. We do not sell personal data. We do not use a merchant's customer list for our own marketing. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 Two different relationships LetBuyy handles personal data in two distinct roles, and your rights differ depending on which one applies. When you hold a LetBuyy merchant account, we are the Data Fiduciary — we decide what is collected and why, and you exercise your rights against us. When you shop at a store built on LetBuyy, that merchant is the Data Fiduciary. We are their Data Processor: we hold the data and act on their instruction. Your rights are exercised against the store, and we support them in answering you. Note If you are not sure which applies: did you sign up at letbuyy.com, or buy something from a store? The first is us; the second is the store. 02 What we collect from merchants To create and operate your account we collect your name, email address, phone number, and password credentials. Passwords are stored hashed and are never recoverable in readable form. To operate your store we hold your business details, GSTIN where you provide one, store configuration, catalogue, and the orders your store receives. To keep the platform working and secure we log requests, errors, and device and network information such as IP address and browser type. Payment credentials are collected by your payment provider, not by us. We hold references and status, not card numbers. 03 What stores collect from shoppers A store typically holds the shopper's name, email, phone, delivery address, order history, and any account credentials created on that storefront. Card details are never held by the store or by us — the payment provider collects them directly and returns only a reference. Each store's data is isolated from every other store at the database level. One merchant cannot read another merchant's customers, and a shopper account on one storefront is not an account on another. 04 Why we process it To provide the service you asked for: running your store, processing orders, computing tax, sending order emails. To keep it secure: detecting fraud, rate-limiting abuse, distinguishing humans from bots at sign-up and login, and investigating incidents. To meet legal obligations: tax records, invoices, and responses to lawful requests. To improve the product, using aggregated and de-identified usage patterns rather than individual records. 05 Consent Where we rely on your consent — optional analytics and marketing communications — it is asked for separately, in plain language, and can be withdrawn as easily as it was given. Withdrawing consent for optional processing does not affect processing we do to deliver the service you are paying for or to meet a legal duty. Cookie choices are managed from the control in the site footer and are covered in detail in the Cookie Policy. 06 Who else sees it Service providers that run parts of the platform — hosting, database, payments, email, shipping, error monitoring. Each is listed in the Sub-processor Register with what it does and where it runs. A merchant's courier and payment provider, to the extent an order requires it. Authorities, where we are legally compelled. We check that a request is valid before responding, and tell the affected person unless the law forbids it. An acquirer, if the business is sold. Notice would be given, and the successor would be bound by this policy until it is properly replaced. Note We do not sell personal data, and we do not share it with advertisers or data brokers. 07 How long we keep it Account and store data is kept while the account is open, and for a limited wind-down period after closure so an accidental closure can be reversed. Orders, invoices, and payment ledger entries are kept for the longer period Indian tax and company law requires, and survive account closure for that reason. Operational telemetry is retained for 90 days. Webhook delivery records are retained for 90 days after reaching a terminal state. When a retention period ends, data is deleted or irreversibly de-identified. 08 Your rights You have the right to know what personal data is held about you and how it is processed; to have inaccurate data corrected; to have data erased where no legal duty requires us to keep it; to withdraw consent for optional processing; and to nominate someone to exercise these rights if you die or become incapacitated. Merchants: exercise these against us at the contact route below, or from your account settings where the action is self-service. Shoppers: exercise these against the store you bought from. If a store will not respond, escalate through our grievance process and we will act. We respond within the time the DPDP Rules require, and will tell you if a legal obligation prevents us from acting on part of a request. 09 How it is protected Data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Tenant isolation is enforced in the database itself, so an application-layer mistake does not expose another store. Actions that move money or change payout destinations require verification beyond a password. The Security Practices page describes the controls in more detail. 10 Children LetBuyy is not intended for children. Merchant accounts require you to be old enough to enter a contract. The DPDP Act requires verifiable parental consent before processing a child's data and prohibits behavioural advertising directed at children. Merchants selling to children are responsible for meeting that standard in their own store. 11 Changes Material changes are notified to account holders by email before they take effect. The revision date at the top of this page always reflects the current text. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . Previous Shipping & Delivery Next Cookie Policy LetBuyy footer LetBuyy What is LetBuyy? Merchants: exercise these against us at the contact route below, or from your account settings where the action is self-service. Shoppers: exercise these against the store you bought from. pages.text: Cookie Policy Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Data & privacy / Cookies Cookie Policy What we store in your browser and what you can turn off. Applies to Everyone Clauses 4 Reading time 1 min Revised 3 August 2026 These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 4 Contents 01 Essential — always on 02 Optional — off until you allow them 03 Cookies on merchant storefronts 04 Changing your choices In short Some cookies are required for the site to work at all — signing in, keeping a cart, blocking bots. Analytics and personalisation are optional and off until you turn them on. You can change your choices at any time from the control in the footer. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 Essential — always on These cannot be turned off because without them the service does not function. Session cookies that keep you signed in to a merchant account or a storefront Cart state, so a shopper does not lose their basket between pages Security tokens that prevent cross-site request forgery Bot-protection tokens set when you register or sign in Load-balancing and routing values that send your request to the right store 02 Optional — off until you allow them Analytics tells us which pages are used and where people get stuck, so we can fix the parts that do not work. Personalisation remembers non-sensitive preferences between visits. Neither is set before you consent, and neither is required to use the site. 03 Cookies on merchant storefronts A storefront may set additional cookies through apps or analytics the merchant has installed. Those are the merchant's choice and are covered by that store's own privacy notice. Merchants are responsible for disclosing what they add. We provide the mechanism, not the decision. 04 Changing your choices Use the privacy control in the footer of any LetBuyy page. Changes apply immediately. Your browser can also block or clear cookies. Blocking essential cookies will break sign-in and checkout — that is a consequence of blocking them, not a fault. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . pages.text: Data Processing Addendum Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Data & privacy / DPA Data Processing Addendum The terms under which LetBuyy processes your shoppers' data for you. Applies to Merchants Clauses 10 Reading time 3 min Revised 3 August 2026 These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 10 Contents 01 Roles 02 Our instructions 03 Confidentiality and access 04 Sub-processors 05 Security measures 06 Personal data breach 07 Helping you answer your shoppers 08 Return and deletion 09 Where data is processed 10 Demonstrating compliance In short When your store holds customer data, you are the Data Fiduciary and LetBuyy is your Processor. We act on your instruction, do not use your customer data for our own purposes, and hold our sub-processors to the same terms. This addendum forms part of your agreement with us and applies automatically — there is nothing to sign. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 Roles You determine what personal data your store collects from shoppers and why. That makes you the Data Fiduciary under the DPDP Act, and the equivalent of a controller under other regimes. We process that data solely to provide the platform to you. That makes us your Processor. We do not decide the purposes and we do not process for our own. 02 Our instructions We process shopper data only as needed to deliver the service, to keep it secure, and where a law compels us. Your configuration of the platform is your instruction. If a legal requirement forces us to process beyond your instruction, we will tell you before doing so unless the law forbids notice. 03 Confidentiality and access Access to production data is limited to personnel who need it, is authenticated individually, and is logged. Everyone with such access is bound by confidentiality obligations that survive the end of their engagement. 04 Sub-processors We use the sub-processors listed in the Sub-processor Register, each bound to obligations no weaker than these. We will give notice before adding a sub-processor that handles shopper personal data, so you have a chance to object. Objecting may mean you cannot continue using the affected feature. We remain responsible to you for our sub-processors' performance. 05 Security measures Encryption in transit and at rest; per-tenant isolation enforced at the database layer; least-privilege access; step-up authentication on money-moving operations; signed webhooks and queue messages; and monitoring of access to production systems. The Security Practices page describes these in more detail. We may improve a measure but will not materially weaken the overall level of protection. 06 Personal data breach If we become aware of a breach affecting your shoppers' data, we will notify you without undue delay with what we know: what happened, what data and how many people are affected, what we are doing, and what you should do. The DPDP Rules require the Data Fiduciary to notify affected individuals and the Board. Since that is you, we will give you what you need to meet that duty on time. 07 Helping you answer your shoppers When a shopper exercises a right against you, we make the underlying data available to you through the dashboard and the APIs so you can answer without needing us in the loop. For anything the tooling does not cover, ask and we will help within the time your legal deadline allows. 08 Return and deletion Export your data at any time while your account is open. Do it before you close the account — that is the point at which it becomes hard. After closure, data is deleted at the end of the wind-down period, except records we are legally required to retain — principally invoices, orders, and ledger entries under tax and company law. Backups age out on their own cycle rather than being individually edited, so deletion from backups completes when the backup expires. 09 Where data is processed We prefer Indian regions for primary data storage. Some sub-processors operate globally distributed infrastructure, and the register states where each one runs. The DPDP Act permits transfer outside India except to countries the government restricts. We will comply with any such restriction if one is notified. 10 Demonstrating compliance We will provide the information reasonably needed to show we meet this addendum. Where an audit right applies, it is exercised on reasonable notice, no more than once a year absent a breach, and without compromising other merchants' data. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . pages.text: Sub-processor Register Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Data & privacy / Sub-processors Sub-processor Register Every third party that touches data on LetBuyy, and what for. Applies to Merchants Clauses 6 Reading time 2 min Revised 3 August 2026 These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 6 Contents 01 Infrastructure and hosting 02 Payments 03 Communications 04 Shipping and logistics 05 Monitoring and operations 06 Changes to this register In short This is the complete list of providers that process data as part of running LetBuyy. Each entry states what it does and whether it can reach personal data. We give notice before adding a sub-processor that handles shopper personal data. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 Infrastructure and hosting These run the platform itself and necessarily hold the data stored in it. Supabase — primary database, authentication storage, and file storage. Holds merchant and shopper personal data. Cloudflare — edge network, DNS, custom-domain routing, bot protection, and the workers that run the API gateway and background jobs. Sees request metadata and traffic in transit. Vercel — hosting for the web applications. Sees request metadata and server logs. 02 Payments Razorpay — payment processing, settlement to merchant bank accounts, and refunds. Collects payment credentials directly from shoppers; we hold references, not card numbers. Razorpay is a Reserve Bank of India authorised payment aggregator and is a Data Fiduciary in its own right for the payment data it collects. 03 Communications Resend — transactional email delivery: order confirmations, account notices, password resets. Processes recipient email addresses and message content. 04 Shipping and logistics Where a merchant connects a courier, that courier receives the delivery address and contact details needed to complete the shipment. Integrations currently available include Shiprocket and Delhivery. These are connected per store by the merchant. A store that does not connect one does not send data to it. 05 Monitoring and operations Sentry — error monitoring. Receives stack traces and request context; configured to scrub credentials and personal data from payloads. Cloudflare Turnstile — bot protection at registration and login. Receives a challenge token and IP address, not account contents. Cloudflare Analytics Engine — aggregated operational metrics. Designed for counts and timings rather than individual records. 06 Changes to this register We will update this page and notify merchant account holders before a new sub-processor that handles shopper personal data begins processing. Removing a sub-processor does not require notice. Note Apps a merchant installs from the marketplace are not our sub-processors. They are separate processors the merchant engages directly, and their data handling is disclosed in their own listing. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . pages.text: Security Practices Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Trust & safety / Security Security Practices How LetBuyy protects merchant and shopper data. Applies to Everyone Clauses 8 Reading time 3 min Revised 3 August 2026 Report a vulnerability Visit the support centre These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 8 Contents 01 Store isolation 02 Money handling 03 Authentication 04 Data in transit and at rest 05 Webhooks and background jobs 06 Internal access 07 Reporting a vulnerability 08 If something goes wrong Store isolation Money handling Authentication In short Store isolation is enforced in the database, not just in application code — an application bug does not expose another merchant. Money movements go through controlled server-side operations with idempotency keys and locks, so a retry cannot double-charge or double-refund. We would rather hear about a vulnerability from you than from an attacker. Reporting one in good faith will not get you sued. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 Store isolation Every record belongs to exactly one store. That boundary is enforced by row-level security in the database, so a query that forgets to filter by store returns nothing rather than everything. This is deliberately belt-and-braces. Application code also checks ownership, but the database is the layer that has to be right, because it is the one an application bug cannot bypass. 02 Money handling Order totals, tax, and shipping are computed on the server from stored configuration. Amounts sent by a browser are never trusted. Every money movement runs through a controlled database operation that takes a lock and requires an idempotency key, so a retried request cannot charge twice or refund twice. Gift-card balances are derived from a ledger of entries rather than stored as a mutable number, so a balance cannot silently drift and cannot go negative. Payment confirmations from the provider are verified by signature on our servers before any order is marked paid. 03 Authentication Merchant sessions and shopper sessions are issued by separate systems with separate signing keys, so a token from one can never be accepted by the other. Passwords are stored hashed. Registration and login are protected by bot challenges and rate limiting. Refunds and payout-destination changes require step-up verification beyond the session — the two operations most worth attacking are the two that ask again. 04 Data in transit and at rest All traffic is served over TLS, including custom domains, for which certificates are provisioned and renewed automatically. Data at rest is encrypted by the storage layer. Credentials for third-party services are held as secrets in the deployment platform and are not present in the codebase. 05 Webhooks and background jobs Inbound webhooks are verified by signature using constant-time comparison before the payload is acted on, and replayed deliveries are rejected. Messages passed to background workers carry a signed tenant envelope, so a job cannot be forged to act against a store it does not belong to. 06 Internal access Access to production data is individually authenticated, limited to those who need it, and logged. Automated checks run on every change to catch a class of mistakes before they merge — including direct writes to money tables, which are structurally forbidden rather than merely discouraged. 07 Reporting a vulnerability Email the security address below with enough detail to reproduce. You will get an acknowledgement, and we will tell you when it is fixed. Please give us reasonable time to fix an issue before disclosing it publicly, do not access or modify data belonging to anyone other than yourself, and stop at proof rather than pivoting further. We will not pursue legal action against a researcher who follows those three things in good faith. Note Do not test against a live merchant's store. If you need an environment to test in, ask us for one. 08 If something goes wrong If a breach affects merchant or shopper data, we will notify affected merchants without undue delay with what happened, what data is involved, and what we are doing about it. Where a merchant must in turn notify their shoppers or the Data Protection Board, we will give them what they need to do that within their own deadline. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . pages.text: Grievance Redressal Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Trust & safety / Grievance Grievance Redressal How to escalate a complaint, and the timelines we hold ourselves to. Applies to Everyone Clauses 6 Reading time 2 min Revised 3 August 2026 How to raise a concern Get support These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 6 Contents 01 Start with the store 02 When to escalate to us 03 How to raise it 04 What happens next 05 What we can and cannot do 06 If you are still not satisfied In short If a store on LetBuyy will not resolve your problem, you can escalate it to us. We acknowledge complaints within 48 hours and work to resolve them within one month, as Indian law requires. Start with the store — it can act on your order directly, which is almost always faster. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. Grievance Officer Published under Rule 4(5), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020 and Rule 3(2), IT (Intermediary Guidelines) Rules 2021. Name To be published at launch Designation To be published at launch Email grievance@letbuyy.com Phone To be published at launch Registered entity To be published at launch LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no officer has been appointed yet. Until one is, complaints sent to the address above reach the team directly and are handled on the same timelines. 48 hours to acknowledge your complaint 1 month to resolve it, or explain the delay 01 Start with the store If your complaint is about an order — it has not arrived, it arrived damaged, a refund has not been issued — contact the store you bought from first. Its contact details are in the storefront footer and on your order confirmation email. The store can see your order, refund it, and reship it. We cannot do those things on their behalf, so going to them first genuinely is faster. 02 When to escalate to us Escalate to LetBuyy when a store has not responded within a reasonable time, refuses to honour its own published policy, appears to be operating fraudulently, or is selling something the Acceptable Use Policy prohibits. Also escalate anything about the platform itself: your account, your data, your payouts, or a security concern. 03 How to raise it Write to the grievance officer at the address published on this page. Include the store name, your order number, what you have already tried, and what outcome you are looking for. Attach evidence where you have it — screenshots, tracking references, and the messages you exchanged with the store. A complaint with evidence gets resolved considerably faster than one without. 04 What happens next We acknowledge receipt within 48 hours, and give you a reference to quote. We work to resolve complaints within one month of receipt. If it will take longer, we will tell you why and when to expect an answer. These are the timelines set by the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020 and the IT Rules 2021. We treat them as deadlines, not targets. 05 What we can and cannot do We can reach a merchant, require them to answer, act against a store that breaks our policies including suspending it, correct anything on the platform side, and give you a clear record of what happened. We cannot compel a merchant to refund you, refund you from our own funds, or reverse a payment your bank has already settled. That boundary follows from the fact that the sale was between you and the merchant. Where it leaves you without a remedy, the consumer forums below can order what we cannot. 06 If you are still not satisfied You can approach the National Consumer Helpline on 1915 or at consumerhelpline.gov.in, or file a complaint with the District, State, or National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission depending on the value of your claim. For a payment dispute your bank or payment provider has not resolved, the RBI Ombudsman scheme is available after you have given the provider 30 days to respond. For a data-protection complaint, you may approach the Data Protection Board of India after raising it with us first. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process .
