pages.text: Intellectual Property & Takedown Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Legal / Trust & safety / IP & takedown Intellectual Property & Takedown Reporting infringement, and what happens when someone reports you. Applies to Everyone Clauses 5 Reading time 2 min Revised 3 August 2026 These policies are published for review and are not yet in force. LetBuyy has not opened to merchants, so no agreement has been formed with anyone. They take effect on the day the platform launches, and the effective date will be stated here. Last revised 3 August 2026. Contents 5 Contents 01 LetBuyy's own marks 02 Your content stays yours 03 Reporting infringement 04 What we do with a report 05 If your listing was removed In short If a store on LetBuyy is infringing your trademark or copyright, tell us and we will act. We act on specific, evidenced reports. A report that cannot identify the listing or the right being infringed cannot be acted on. If your listing is removed, you will be told why and can respond. This summary is written to be understood. The clauses below are what actually applies — where the two differ, the clauses govern. 01 LetBuyy's own marks The LetBuyy name, logo, and product names are ours. You may refer to LetBuyy accurately — "built on LetBuyy" is fine — but may not use our marks in a way that suggests we endorse, sponsor, or operate your business. You may not use our marks in your domain name, app name, or logo without written permission. 02 Your content stays yours Your catalogue, photography, copy, and brand remain yours. Publishing them through LetBuyy grants us only the licence needed to host and serve them, which ends when you remove them. 03 Reporting infringement Send a report to the contact route below containing all of the following. A report missing any of it will be sent back rather than actioned, because we cannot act on an unidentifiable claim. The specific right you hold, with a registration number where one exists Evidence you own it or are authorised to act for the owner The exact URL of each infringing listing or page An explanation of why it infringes A statement that you believe in good faith that the use is not authorised Your name, address, and a working contact route 04 What we do with a report We review it, and where it is complete and appears well-founded we remove or disable the listing and tell the merchant what was removed and who reported it. We do not adjudicate ownership. Where two parties both claim a right, we may keep content down until they resolve it between themselves or a court decides. Merchants who receive repeated substantiated reports lose access. 05 If your listing was removed You will be told what was removed and on what basis. If you believe the report was wrong, reply with your evidence — a licence, your own registration, or an explanation of why the use is permitted. Where a counter-notice is credible we may restore the listing and tell the original reporter, who can then take it up directly with you. Note Knowingly filing a false infringement report to damage a competitor is itself actionable. We keep records of who reported what. Questions about this document Write to support@letbuyy.com and quote the clause number. For a complaint rather than a question, use the grievance process . UPI + COD + அட்டைகள் தானியங்கி GST விலைப்பட்டியல் Razorpay இணைப்பு வாடிக்கையாளர்கள் சுயவிவரம், விசுவாசம், புரிதல்கள் நேரலை வாங்குதல் வரலாறு, மதிப்புரை, நடத்தைப் பிரிவுகளுடன் வாடிக்கையாளர் சுயவிவரம் உருவாக்குங்கள். தளத்திலிருந்தே தக்கவைப்பு இயக்கங்கள் நடத்துங்கள். வாடிக்கையாளர் சுயவிவரங்கள் வாங்குதல் வரலாறும் மதிப்புரைகளும் பிரிவுகள் மற்றும் தக்கவைப்பு பகுப்பாய்வு எப்போதும் வருவாய் நுண்ணறிவு நேரலை வருவாய், விற்பனை மாற்றம், தயாரிப்புச் செயல்திறனைக் கண்காணியுங்கள். உண்மையான வணிகத் தரவிலிருந்து தினசரிச் சுருக்கமும் நேரடி முகப்பும். வருவாயும் விற்பனை மாற்றமும் தயாரிப்புச் செயல்திறன் வாடிக்கையாளர் போக்குகள் AI இயக்குநர் மற்றும் தானியக்கம் தானியங்கி வணிகச் செயல்பாடுகள் நுண்ணறிவு AI செயல்பாடு: தயாரிப்பு விளக்கம் உருவாக்கம், தேவை முன்னறிவிப்பு, மோசடி ஆர்டர் கண்டறிதல், மாறும் விலை மேம்பாடு. SEOக்கு ஏற்ற தயாரிப்பு உரை, படங்களுக்கான உருவாக்க AI விற்பனை வரலாறு, பருவநிலையின் அடிப்படையில் தேவை முன்னறிவிப்பு ஒவ்வொரு ஆர்டருக்கும் மோசடி, RTO முன்னறிவிப்பு மதிப்பெண் ஆர்டர் கண்காணிப்பு, பொதுக் LetBuyy உங்கள் இணையக் கடை, ஆர்டர்கள், வாடிக்கையாளர் கருவிகளை ஒரே இடத்தில் இணைக்கிறது. தொடக்கம் முதல் அடுத்த தொகுப்புவரை இவை உதவும் விதம் இதோ. 01 உங்களுக்கேற்றதாக்குங்கள் உங்கள் பொருட்கள். உங்கள் இணையக் கடை. உங்கள் பிராண்டுடன் கைபேசி, டேப்லெட், கணினியில் இயங்கும் இணையக் கடையை உருவாக்குங்கள். தீமைத் தேர்ந்து உங்களுக்கேற்றதாக்குங்கள். படங்கள், விலை, அளவுகள், இருப்பைச் சேர்க்கவும். முன்னோட்டம் பார்த்து டொமைனை இணைத்து வெளியிடுங்கள். கடைமுகத் தீம்களை ஆராயுங்கள் 02 விற்கத் தொடங்குங்கள் வாடிக்கையாளர் கூடையிலிருந்து பொதிந்த ஆர்டர் வரை. கடை இணைப்பைப் பகிருங்கள். வாடிக்கையாளர் பார்த்து வாங்கியபின் பணியிடத்திலிருந்து ஒவ்வொரு ஆர்டரையும் கையாளுங்கள். நீங்கள் இயக்கிய பணமுறைகளை வழங்குங்கள். வாங்குதல், பண நிலை, இருப்பை ஒன்றாகப் பாருங்கள். அனுப்புதலைத் தயாரித்து கண்காணிப்பைச் சேர்த்து திருப்புதலைக் கையாளுங்கள். ஆர்டர் நிறைவேற்றத்தை அறியுங்கள் 03 மீண்டும் வரச் செய்யுங்கள் முதல் வாங்குதலை உறவாக்குங்கள். வாங்குபவரை அறிந்து அடுத்த தொகுப்பைப் பகிர்ந்து விற்பனை அறிக்கையால் அடுத்ததைத் தீர்மானியுங்கள். வாடிக்கையாளர் சுயவிவரம், வாங்குதல் வரலாற்றைக் காணுங்கள். சந்தா வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்கான மின்னஞ்சல் இயக்கம் தயாரிக்கவும். அடுத்த திட்டத்திற்கு ஆர்டர்கள், வருவாயைப் பாருங்கள். மின்னஞ்சல் சந்தைப்படுத்தல் வழிகாட்டியைப் படிக்கவும் பணப்பரிவர்த்தனை, அனுப்புதல், மின்னஞ்சல் உங்கள் திட்டம், கணக்கு அமைப்பு, இணைந்த வழங்குநர்களைப் பொறுத்தவை. அன்றாட எடுத்துக்காட்டு ஒரு டி-ஷர்ட் விற்கப்பட்டது. அடுத்த படிகள், ஒன்றாக. வாடிக்கையாளர் உங்கள் கடையில் நீல டி-ஷர்ட் வாங்குகிறார். ஒரே இடத்தில் ஆர்டர் விவரங்களுடன் அடுத்த வேலையைப் பின்தொடருங்கள். 01 ஆர்டரைப் பார்க்கவும் பொருள், வாங்குபவர், விநியோக விவரங்கள் ஒன்றாக. 02 பணப்பரிவர்த்தனையைச் சரிபார்க்கவும் பணம் செலுத்தப்பட்டதா, நிலுவையா, CODஆ என அறியுங்கள். 03 இருப்பைச் சரியாக வைத்திருங்கள் அடுத்த விற்பனைக்கு முன் இருப்பைப் பார்க்கவும். 04 விநியோகத்தைத் தயாரிக்கவும் ஆர்டரைப் பொதிந்து அனுப்புதல் நிலையைப் புதுப்பியுங்கள். உங்கள் நாளுக்கு இதன் பொருள் என்ன? செய்ய வேண்டிய வேலையிலிருந்து தொடங்குங்கள். ஒரு ஆர்டர் வருகிறது + பொருள், வாடிக்கையாளர், பணம், விநியோக விவரங்களுக்கு ஆர்டரைத் திறக்கவும். தயாரிப்பிலிருந்து விநியோகம் வரை பின்தொடரவும். பணப்பரிவர்த்தனையைச் சரிபார்க்க வேண்டும் + ஆர்டரின் பண நிலை, பரிவர்த்தனை விவரங்களைப் பார்க்கவும். இணையப் பணம், CODஐத் தனித்தனியாகப் பின்தொடரலாம். வாடிக்கையாளருக்குப் பணத்திருப்பம் தேவை + பணியிடத்தில் ஆர்டர், பணத்திருப்ப விவரங்களைப் பார்க்கவும். முடிந்ததாகக் கருதாமல் இணைந்த பண வழங்குநரில் நிலையைச் சரிபார்க்கவும். ஒரு தயாரிப்பு குறைகிறது + ஒவ்வொரு பொருள், மாறுபாட்டின் அளவு, இருப்பு வரலாற்றைப் பார்த்து மீள் இருப்பு அல்லது கொள்முதல் ஆர்டர் தயாரிக்கவும். புதிய தொகுப்பைப் பகிர வேண்டும் + மின்னஞ்சல் இயக்கம் உருவாக்கி சந்தா வாடிக்கையாளர் அல்லது பிரிவைத் தேர்ந்து பெறுநர், செய்தியைச் சரிபார்த்து அனுப்பவும். உண்மையான அனுப்புதலுக்கு மின்னஞ்சல் அமைப்பு தேவை. வருமானத்தைப் புரிந்துகொள்ள வேண்டும் + விற்பனை, பணம், பணத்திருப்பம், தீர்வு விவரங்களைப் பார்க்கவும். வழங்குநரின் செயலாக்கம், தீர்வு நேரம் ஆர்டர் பதிவிலிருந்து வேறானது. விலை எளிய, வெளிப்படையான விலை Launch, Growth இப்போது உள்ளன. Scale, Commerce OS விரைவில். பரிவர்த்தனை, தளக் கட்டணம் என்றும் 0%. அடிக்கடி கேட்கப்படும் கேள்விகள் தொடங்குமுன் அறிய வேண்டிய அனைத்தும் விலை, இடமாற்றம், பணப்பரிவர்த்தனை, தரவு உரிமை, பிற தளங்களுடனான LetBuyy ஒப்பீட்டுக்கான பதில்கள். நவீன வணிகத்திற்காக உருவாக்கப்பட்டது பரிவர்த்தனை கமிஷன் இல்லை இந்தியப் பணப்பரிவர்த்தனை அமைப்பு தனிப்பயன் டொமைன் ஆதரவு இடமாற்ற உதவி உள்ளது AI இயல்பான வணிகத் தளம் AI திறன்கள் 50+ கண்காணிப்பு 24/7 தரவு உரிமை 100% கமிஷன் 0% LetBuyy என்றால் என்ன? LetBuyy சூழலமைப்பு ஒரே தளம். பல வலுவான பணிப்பரப்புகள். இணைந்த சூழலிலிருந்து வணிகம் நடத்த வணிகர், உருவாக்குநர், இயக்குநர், கூட்டாளிகளுக்குத் தேவையான அனைத்தும். 12+ தளப் பணிப்பரப்புகள் 1 ஒருங்கிணைந்த அடையாளம் 100% வணிக இயக்கம் AI இயல்பான அடித்தளம் மையத் தளம் வணிகர் கட்டுப்பாட்டு மையம் ஒவ்வொரு LetBuyy கடைக்குப் பின்னுள்ள இயக்க அமைப்பு. தயாரிப்புகள் ஆர்டர்கள் இருப்பு வாடிக்கையாளர்கள் பகுப்பாய்வு AI துணையாளர் urban-kicks.letbuyy.com முன்னோட்டம் தயாரிப்புகள் ஆர்டர்கள் இருப்பு பணப்பரிவர்த்தனை வாடிக்கையாளர்கள் பகுப்பாய்வு AI துணையாளர் ₹84.2K வருவாய் 248 ஆர்டர்கள் 99.2% பணப்பரிவர்த்தனை 3.9% மாற்றம் Order ORD-4821 shipped · Air Classic AI: Restock Everyday Hoodie — 7 units left Payment confirmed · ₹2,999 via UPI கட்டுப்பாட்டு மையத்தைத் திறக்கவும் தளப் பணிப்பரப்புகள் தீம்கள் கடைமுக தீம் வழிகாட்டி வழிகாட்டி செயலிகள் செயலி இணைப்பு வழிகாட்டி வழிகாட்டி உருவாக்குநர்கள் API, webhook, OAuth, SDK வழிகாட்டி விலை நிறுவனர் மற்றும் வளர்ச்சித் திட்டங்கள் திட்டங்கள் அனைத்துப் பணிப்பரப்புகளும் ஒரே வணிக இயக்கம், அடையாளம், தரவு அடுக்கைப் பகிர்கின்றன. இன்றே LetBuyy உடன் உருவாக்கத் தொடங்குங்கள். நிமிடங்களில் கடை, வலைப்பதிவு அல்லது அறிமுகப் பக்கத்தைத் தொடங்குங்கள். இலவசமாகத் தொடங்குங்கள் செயல்விளக்கம் கோரவும் கிரெடிட் அட்டை தேவையில்லை • என்றும் இலவசத் திட்டம் உள்ளது

headings.text: स्टोर से बढ़कर। आपका कॉमर्स OS।
आपके व्यवसाय की हर ज़रूरत। एक ऑपरेटिंग सिस्टम।
पहले दिन से अगले बड़े कदम तक।
अपनी पहचान दें। फिर शुरुआत करें।
पहले खरीदार को लौटने की वजह दें।
ग्राहक की कार्ट से पैक किए ऑर्डर तक।
पहली खरीद को रिश्ते में बदलें।
एक टी-शर्ट बिकी।अगले कदम, एक साथ।
आपके दिन के काम में इसका मतलब?
शुरुआत से पहले जानने योग्य बातें
LetBuyy Shopify से अलग कैसे है?
क्या अपना कस्टम डोमेन इस्तेमाल कर सकता हूँ?
LetBuyy में कौन से भुगतान विकल्प हैं?
क्या Shopify, WooCommerce या दूसरे प्लेटफ़ॉर्म से आ सकता हूँ?
क्या LetBuyy बढ़ते व्यवसाय के लिए सही है?
क्या लेनदेन पर कमीशन लेते हैं?
मुफ़्त परीक्षण के बाद क्या होगा?
स्टोर डेटा का मालिक कौन है?
आज ही LetBuyy के साथ शुरुआत करें।

कॉमर्स OS। आधुनिक कॉमर्स के एक ही प्लेटफ़ॉर्म से स्टोरफ़्रंट, स्टॉक, ऑर्डर, भुगतान, विश्लेषण, AI, B2B और संचालन चलाएँ। मुफ़्त शुरू करें क्षमताएँ देखें हमेशा 0% कमीशन UPI अंतर्निहित GST के लिए तैयार AI संचालित भारत के लिए बना 0% हमेशा शून्य कमीशन 14 दिन मुफ़्त परीक्षण UPI+COD भुगतान तैयार कॉमर्स OS प्लेटफ़ॉर्म एक बार चलने वाला उदाहरण: तमिलनाडु का नक्शा भारत और फिर बिंदुओं वाले ग्लोब में बदलता है। भारत, पाकिस्तान, चीन, जापान और अन्य महाद्वीपों पर स्टोर दिखते हैं। अंत में बिंदु फैलते हैं और “LetBuyy — दुनिया भर में बेचें” शीर्षक हल्की झिलमिलाहट के बाद स्थिर होता है। कम गति पसंद करने वालों को बिना ऐनिमेशन अंतिम शीर्षक दिखता है। यह दोबारा नहीं चलता। यह उदाहरण है, लाइव व्यापारी डेटा नहीं। रोकने के लिए चित्र पर होवर या फ़ोकस करें। स्टोर बना Tamil Nadu, India स्टोर बना Bengaluru, India स्टोर क्षमता मानचित्र आपके व्यवसाय की हर ज़रूरत। एक ऑपरेटिंग सिस्टम। एक प्लेटफ़ॉर्म से स्टोरफ़्रंट, ऑर्डर, स्टॉक, भुगतान, विश्लेषण, AI, B2B और संचालन चलाएँ। COMMERCE OS स्टोरफ़्रंट ऑर्डर स्टॉक भुगतान ग्राहक विश्लेषण AI B2B स्वचालित मॉड्यूल यात्रा रोकें बाएँ-दाएँ स्वाइप करें, तीर वाली कुंजी दबाएँ या मानचित्र में मॉड्यूल चुनें। छूने पर अपने आप बदलना रुकता है। स्टोरफ़्रंट आपका ब्रांड, हर जगह लाइव कस्टम Explore five moments in a growing business—and the LetBuyy tools you can use at each one. 01 Launch Store Launch 02 First Order Sell 03 Scale Operations Operate 04 Build Brand Retain 05 Enterprise Expand Storefronts + Themes Make it yours. Then open the doors. Turn your products into a storefront that feels like your business. Start with the essentials and publish when you are ready. Shape your storefront Choose a theme, adjust your branding and preview it on different screens. Prepare your catalogue Add product photos, prices, sizes and available stock. Make it easy to find Use your LetBuyy address or connect an eligible custom domain. Orders + Payments Your first sale. A clear next step. When a customer buys, bring the order, payment and delivery details together. Follow the work from purchase to a prepared parcel. Review the purchase See what was ordered, who bought it and where it needs to go. Follow the payment Check whether the order is paid, pending or cash on delivery. Prepare the parcel Pack the items, add shipment details and follow delivery progress. Inventory + Orders More orders. A more organised day. Keep the stockroom and the order list working together. Know what is available, what needs attention and what is ready to leave. Know your stock Review available quantities for each product and variant. Plan a restock Check stock history and prepare incoming inventory or purchase orders. Keep fulfilment moving Follow pending orders, shipment updates and returns in your workspace. Customers + Analytics Give a first-time buyer a reason to return. Get to know your customers and plan your next collection with better context. Build the relationship beyond one transaction. Understand your customers Find customer profiles, purchase history and useful segments. Share the next collection Prepare email campaigns for customers who have subscribed. Learn from your sales Review product performance and revenue before planning your next move. B2B + AI + Analytics A wider business. A connected workspace. As the business becomes more complex, bring wholesale work, AI assistance and reporting into the same operating picture. Organise wholesale work Manage business buyers and bulk-order workflows alongside your retail operations. Work with AI assistance Prepare supported content drafts and review suggestions before acting. Keep the wider view Use your commerce reports to understand the business across its activities. Previous 01 / 05 Next stage Tools depend on your plan and setup. Payments, shipping and live email delivery require the relevant provider connections. How LetBuyy works Build your store. Run the business behind it. LetBuyy brings your online shop, orders and customer tools into one workspace. Here’s how they help you, from opening day to your next collection. 01 Make it yours Your products. Your own online store. Give your business a home online, with your branding and a storefront that works on phones, tablets and computers. Choose a theme and make it your own. Add product photos, prices, sizes and stock. Preview your shop, connect your domain and publish. Explore storefront themes 02 Start selling From a customer’s basket to a packed order. Share your store link. Let customers browse and buy, then manage each order from your merchant workspace. Offer the payment methods you have enabled. See purchases, payment status and stock together. Prepare shipments, add tracking and handle returns. See how order fulfilment works 03 Keep them coming back Turn a first purchase into a relationship. Understand who buys from you, share your next collection and use your sales reports to decide what to do next. Find customer profiles and purchase history. Prepare email campaigns for subscribed customers. Review orders and revenue to plan your next move. Read the email marketing guide Payment, shipping and email options depend on your plan, account setup and connected providers. An everyday example One T-shirt sold. The next steps, together. A customer buys a navy T-shirt from your store. Follow the work that comes next, with the order details in one place. 01 See the order The products, buyer and delivery details are together. 02 Check the payment Know whether it is paid, pending or cash on delivery. 03 Keep stock accurate Review available quantities before the next sale. 04 Prepare delivery Pack the order and keep shipment progress up to date. What does that mean for your day? Start with the job you need to do. An order comes in + Open the order to see the items, customer, payment and delivery details. Follow its progress from preparation through delivery. A payment needs checking + Look at the order’s payment status and transaction details. An online payment and a cash-on-delivery order can be followed separately. A customer needs a refund + Review the order and refund details in your workspace. Follow the refund status through your connected payment provider rather than assuming it has completed. A product is running low + Check quantities for each product and variant, review stock history and prepare a restock or purchase order. You have a new collection to share + Create an email campaign, choose subscribed customers or a customer segment, preview the audience and review the message before sending. Live email delivery requires email setup. You want to understand your earnings + Review sales, payments, refunds and available settlement information. Payment-provider processing and settlement timing are separate from an order being placed. Pricing Simple, transparent pricing Launch and Growth plans are live now. Scale and Commerce OS are coming soon. 0% transaction and platform fees — forever. pages.text: How Themes Work on LetBuyy | LetBuyy Resources Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Resources All Ecommerce Growth Payments Operations AI Commerce Developers Changelog Commerce updates Contents 01 Theme Types 02 The Theme Editor 03 Sections: Modular Page Building 04 Publishing Changes 9 min read Updated Jun 2026 Share Print Back to Resources Resources › Platform How Themes Work on LetBuyy The technical and merchant guide to themes, customization, and the theme engine. L LetBuyy Team Platform 20 Apr 2026 9 min read Updated 11 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # themes # storefront # customization # platform THE STOREFRONT DESIGN STUDIO Your brand. Every detail. One design layer. A storefront that feels like you. Designed around your business Your theme is your storefront's design layer. It controls layout, typography, colors, animations, and how products and collections are displayed. LetBuyy themes come in three flavors: free, marketplace, and custom. 01 Choose your foundation Theme Types Free Themes: Maintained by LetBuyy — Clarity, Urban Kicks, Minimal, Grid Marketplace Themes: Built by third-party developers, reviewed by LetBuyy, paid or free Custom Themes: Built by your team or an agency, uploaded directly to your store 02 Make it your own The Theme Editor Desktop preview Draft Customize Make it your own COLORS TYPOGRAPHY Aa Brand type SECTIONS Header Hero image Product grid Illustrative editor layout · preview on the left, customization on the right. Open Storefront → Theme Editor from your dashboard. You'll see a live preview of your store on the left and customization panels on the right. Changes are previewed in real time before you save. Colors: Primary, secondary, text, background, border colors Typography: Font family, sizes, and weights per element Sections: Reorder, hide, and configure homepage sections Header/Footer: Navigation, logo, social links Product Cards: Layout, image aspect ratio, info shown 03 Build your pages Sections: Modular Page Building 01 Hero image 02 Product grid 03 Image with text 04 Newsletter signup Every theme page is built from sections — modular blocks that can be reordered, duplicated, and configured. Common sections: Hero image, Product grid, Testimonials, Image with text, Video embed, Newsletter signup, FAQs. 04 Bring it to life Publishing Changes Draft Only you Preview Your team Published Your visitors Theme changes have three states: Draft (only you see it), Preview (share via preview link for team review), and Published (live for all visitors). Always preview before publishing. Theme Backups Before any major theme change, duplicate your theme as a backup (Theme Actions → Duplicate). If something breaks, swap back to the backup in one click. R Ravi Krishnan Operations 25 Mar 2026 9 min read Updated 8 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # fulfillment # orders # operations # scaling The guide, illustrated Follow the work from available stock to a prepared parcel and delivery. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 The workflow 02 Pack 03 Dispatch The Fulfillment Workflow Order received and payment confirmed (auto) · Order routed to fulfillment location (auto) Read this section Packing Station Setup A well-organized packing station reduces per-order packing time from 8 minutes to 2 minutes. Essentials: thermal label printer (direct thermal, no ink needed), box and poly-bag sizes matched to your SKUs, packaging tape gun, void fill (paper not bubble wrap — cheaper and branded), and pre-printed invoice stack for the day's orders. Read this section Courier Integration LetBuyy integrates directly with Shiprocket, Delhivery, and BlueDart. When you confirm an order, the shipping label is automatically generated with buyer address, weight, and order value. AWB tracking updates automatically to your store and buyer. Read this section The difference between a hobby store and a real business is operational consistency. Buyers forgive one bad experience. Repeat bad experiences end brands. Order fulfillment is where your brand promise meets operational reality. The Fulfillment Workflow The workflow Understand what is in stock, where it belongs and what needs attention. Concept illustration Order received and payment confirmed (auto) Order routed to fulfillment location (auto) Pick: staff picks item from warehouse shelf Pack: item packaged with invoice, inserts, branding Label: shipping label generated and applied Dispatch: handed to courier for pickup or dropped at facility Track: AWB updated in system, customer notified via WhatsApp/email Packing Station Setup A well-organized packing station reduces per-order packing time from 8 minutes to 2 minutes. Essentials: thermal label printer (direct thermal, no ink needed), box and poly-bag sizes matched to your SKUs, packaging tape gun, void fill (paper not bubble wrap — cheaper and branded), and pre-printed invoice stack for the day's orders. Batch Processing Don't fulfill orders one by one. Batch print all labels for the morning courier pickup. Pick all items for the batch together. Pack together. This reduces per-order time by 40%. Courier Integration Dispatch Follow the work from available stock to a prepared parcel and delivery. Concept illustration LetBuyy integrates directly with Shiprocket, Delhivery, and BlueDart. When you confirm an order, the shipping label is automatically generated with buyer address, weight, and order value. AWB tracking updates automatically to your store and buyer. P Priya Sharma Commerce Lead 1 May 2026 12 min read Updated 15 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # store-setup # india # beginners # gst The guide, illustrated Choose a theme, prepare your products, and bring your store to life. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Plan 02 Build 03 Launch Step 1: Decide What You're Selling Before touching a single platform, clarify your product-market fit. The best-performing Indian D2C stores in 2026 fall into three buckets: high-margin branded goods (fashion, beauty, supplements), regionally-authentic products (handlooms, artisan crafts, regional foods), and business supplies (stationery, packaging, tools). Read this section Step 4: Set Up Your Store On LetBuyy, the onboarding flow walks you through every critical step: store name and domain, theme selection, product upload, payment setup, shipping zones, and GST configuration — in one connected flow. Read this section Step 7: Launch and Validate Don't aim for perfection before launch. Aim for your first 10 orders. Real customer feedback is worth more than any amount of internal testing. Launch to your existing network first — WhatsApp groups, Instagram, college alumni networks — before spending on ads. Read this section India's ecommerce market crossed ₹5 lakh crore in 2025 and is projected to triple by 2030. Yet most guides about starting an online store are written for Shopify merchants in the US — they skip GST, ignore COD, and assume everyone uses Stripe. This guide doesn't. India Ecommerce Market ₹5L Cr+ ↑ 28% YoY UPI Share of Payments 65% ↑ from 48% in 2023 Tier 2/3 City Buyers 71% of new D2C customers Step 1: Decide What You're Selling Plan Show the product clearly, then help the buyer decide. Concept illustration Before touching a single platform, clarify your product-market fit. The best-performing Indian D2C stores in 2026 fall into three buckets: high-margin branded goods (fashion, beauty, supplements), regionally-authentic products (handlooms, artisan crafts, regional foods), and business supplies (stationery, packaging, tools). Key Insight Undersaturated categories win in Tier 2 India Categories that are oversaturated globally — like candles, phone cases, or basic apparel — often have 5–10 years of real runway in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities where organized ecommerce barely exists. The competition you're benchmarking against is local offline retail, not Amazon. India Advantage Categories that are oversaturated globally — like candles or phone cases — often have real runway in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities where organized ecommerce barely exists. Step 2: Get Your Legal and GST Setup Right You need a GSTIN before you can sell on most platforms or accept online payments at scale. Registration takes 7–10 working days through the GST portal. You'll need your PAN, Aadhaar, bank account details, and a business address. GST Registration Checklist PAN card of the business owner or entity Aadhaar card for identity verification Bank account statement or cancelled cheque Proof of business address (rent agreement or utility bill) Digital signature certificate (for company/LLP) MOA/AOA if registering a Private Limited company Sole proprietor: No separate registration needed. GST under your PAN. Partnership / LLP: Register with MCA first, then GST. Private Limited: Recommended for brands expecting VC or large scale. Don't Skip This If your annual turnover exceeds ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh in special category states), GST registration is mandatory. Even below that, voluntary registration unlocks input tax credit — a significant cost advantage. Step 3: Choose Your Platform Your platform is your commerce operating system. It affects everything: your checkout experience, theme flexibility, payment gateway options, and how much time you spend on operations vs. growth. Platform Best For India Payment Support GST Invoicing LetBuyy India-first brands of all sizes ✓ Native UPI + COD + Razorpay ✓ Auto-generated Shopify Global brands with India presence ✓ Via third-party apps ⚠ Plugin required Dukaan Very small / single-SKU sellers ✓ Basic ⚠ Limited WooCommerce Technical teams with custom needs ✓ Manual setup ⚠ Plugin required Commerce Example A Jaipur-based kurta brand switched from Shopify to LetBuyy in April 2026. Their checkout had 3 steps instead of 7, UPI worked without a redirect, and GST invoices generated automatically. Cart completion rate went from 34% to 61% in 60 days. COD orders from Tier 2 cities doubled. +79% checkout conversion Step 4: Set Up Your Store On LetBuyy, the onboarding flow walks you through every critical step: store name and domain, theme selection, product upload, payment setup, shipping zones, and GST configuration — in one connected flow. 1 01 Create your account Sign up at accounts.letbuyy.com with your business email. Takes under 2 minutes. 2 02 Name and configure your store Choose a subdomain (yourstore.letbuyy.com) or connect a custom domain you already own. 3 03 Select and customize your theme Pick from 40+ India-ready themes in the marketplace. Mobile-first layouts, fast-loading, conversion-optimized. 4 04 Upload your first product Add title, description, price, variants (size/color), and inventory count. Bulk CSV import available. 5 05 Configure payments Enable UPI via Razorpay and COD. Both take under 10 minutes to activate. No manual bank integration required. 6 06 Set up shipping zones and GST Define rates for local, state, and all-India delivery. Enter your GSTIN once — invoices auto-generate forever. Step 5: Configure Payments Indian buyers have strong payment preferences that differ significantly from Western markets. In 2026, UPI accounts for 65% of online transactions, COD remains at 30% for Tier 2+ cities, and cards cover the remainder. UPI 65% of online transactions Cash on Delivery 30% Tier 2/3 dominant Cards & Wallets 5% Metro-heavy COD Strategy Don't view COD as a burden — view it as your Tier 2 and Tier 3 city unlock. Brands that disable COD lose up to 40% of addressable revenue in India. Offer it, but set a ₹2,000 order minimum to manage return risk. Step 6: Sort Your Logistics Shipping is where most new Indian stores fail silently. Choose a courier partner with strong Tier 2 and Tier 3 coverage — not just metro cities. Look for NDR (non-delivery report) automation, real-time tracking, and RTO (return to origin) rates under 15%. AI Recommendation How to choose the right courier partner for your stage Under ₹50K monthly GMV: Use Shiprocket. Aggregates 17+ couriers, no volume minimums, simple dashboard. ₹50K–₹5L GMV: Negotiate directly with Delhivery. Better per-shipment rates and Tier 2 coverage than aggregators. ₹5L+ GMV: Split across 2 couriers. Delhivery for volume + BlueDart for high-value or time-sensitive orders. RTO above 20%: This is a marketing problem, not a logistics problem. Tighten your targeting before scaling. Shiprocket: Best aggregator for small volumes (<500 shipments/month) Delhivery: Strong for Tier 2/3 coverage, enterprise pricing starts lower BlueDart: Premium, metro-heavy, great for high-value goods DTDC: Widest PIN code coverage in India Step 7: Launch and Validate Launch Follow the work from available stock to a prepared parcel and delivery. Concept illustration Don't aim for perfection before launch. Aim for your first 10 orders. Real customer feedback is worth more than any amount of internal testing. Launch to your existing network first — WhatsApp groups, Instagram, college alumni networks — before spending on ads. Pre-Launch Checklist Test checkout end-to-end on mobile (iPhone and Android) Place a real test order with UPI and verify GST invoice Check that all product images load fast on 4G Set up WhatsApp Business number for support Write 5 WhatsApp messages to send to your first potential buyers Announce on Instagram Story with swipe-up link to store First 10 Orders Milestone Getting 10 orders from people who don't know you personally is the single most important validation milestone for any Indian D2C brand. Everything before that is planning. Everything after that is execution. N Neha Gupta Payments & Compliance 5 Apr 2026 9 min read Updated 14 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # payments # upi # cod # india The guide, illustrated Two payment paths, one customer journey: pay digitally or pay on delivery. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 UPI 02 Cash on delivery 03 Payment mix UPI: The Dominant Force UPI crossed 1 billion daily transactions in 2025. For ecommerce, it's the ideal payment method: instant settlement, zero failure rates vs. cards, and zero fee for amounts under ₹2,000. The challenge is UPI app switching on mobile browsers — which creates a 3–5% drop-off that deep links partially solve. Read this section COD: The Trust Bridge COD exists because trust in online stores takes time to build. First-time buyers, buyers in markets with weak digital financial infrastructure, and high-value fashion buyers who need to "see before they pay" all depend on COD. The return rate is real — but so is the revenue. Read this section The Optimal Payment Mix Strategy Don't choose between UPI and COD. Offer both, but design your funnel to guide buyers toward prepaid: "Pay now and get free shipping" is the most effective nudge. UPI prepaid orders cost less to fulfill, settle instantly, and return at one-third the rate of COD. Read this section No payment debate is more Indian than UPI vs COD. Both are distinctly India-first. Both are essential. And most brands get the balance wrong. The State of Indian Payments in 2026 Method Market Share Avg Order Value Return Rate Best For UPI 65% ₹1,200 8% Metro, repeat buyers, digital natives COD 29% ₹780 22% Tier 2/3, first-time buyers, fashion Cards 5% ₹2,400 4% High-value, B2B, subscriptions Wallets 1% ₹650 3% Low-value, impulse purchases UPI: The Dominant Force UPI Two payment paths, one customer journey: pay digitally or pay on delivery. Concept illustration UPI crossed 1 billion daily transactions in 2025. For ecommerce, it's the ideal payment method: instant settlement, zero failure rates vs. cards, and zero fee for amounts under ₹2,000. The challenge is UPI app switching on mobile browsers — which creates a 3–5% drop-off that deep links partially solve. UPI Deep Links LetBuyy's checkout uses UPI intent links that open the buyer's preferred UPI app directly (PhonePe, GPay, Paytm, BHIM) without manual entry. This reduces UPI drop-off by 2–4%. COD: The Trust Bridge COD exists because trust in online stores takes time to build. First-time buyers, buyers in markets with weak digital financial infrastructure, and high-value fashion buyers who need to "see before they pay" all depend on COD. The return rate is real — but so is the revenue. Reducing COD Return Rates Require phone number verification (OTP) for COD orders above ₹1,000 Block COD for PIN codes with >30% RTO history Send a pre-delivery WhatsApp confirmation (reduces RTO by 15%) Charge a ₹50–100 COD convenience fee for orders under ₹500 Use NDR automation to reattempt delivery within 24 hours The Optimal Payment Mix Strategy Payment mix Follow the work from available stock to a prepared parcel and delivery. Concept illustration Don't choose between UPI and COD. Offer both, but design your funnel to guide buyers toward prepaid: "Pay now and get free shipping" is the most effective nudge. UPI prepaid orders cost less to fulfill, settle instantly, and return at one-third the rate of COD. pages.text: How to Get Your First 100 Orders | LetBuyy Resources Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Resources All Ecommerce Growth Payments Operations AI Commerce Developers Changelog Commerce updates Contents 01 Why 100 Orders is the Magic Number 02 Orders 1–10: Your Personal Network 03 Orders 10–50: Community and WhatsApp Groups 04 Orders 50–100: Instagram Organic and Influencer Seeding 05 Retain the First 100: The Thank You Advantage 10 min read Updated Jun 2026 Share Print Back to Resources Resources › Growth Featured How to Get Your First 100 Orders A tactical playbook for new Indian D2C brands — no ad budget required. P Priya Sharma Commerce Lead 15 May 2026 10 min read Updated 15 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # growth # beginners # organic # whatsapp The guide, illustrated Build relationships from the first introduction to the next order. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Your network 02 Community 03 Keep customers Orders 1–10: Your Personal Network Your first 10 orders should come from people who know you. Not because they're doing you a favor — but because getting them to pay full price validates that your positioning works. If people who like you won't pay for it, strangers definitely won't. Read this section Orders 10–50: Community and WhatsApp Groups India has the world's most active WhatsApp group ecosystem. Local resident welfare groups, college alumni chats, professional networks, hobby groups — all of them are potential buyers for the right product. Read this section Retain the First 100: The Thank You Advantage Your first 100 buyers are your founding community. Treat them like it. A handwritten note in the package, a personal WhatsApp follow-up 5 days post-delivery, a referral incentive before they've moved on — these are low-cost actions with outsized loyalty returns. Read this section Your first 100 orders are the hardest. Not because the market is saturated — but because you have no social proof, no word-of-mouth, and no algorithm working for you yet. Everything is activation energy. This guide shows you how to build it. Why 100 Orders is the Magic Number At 100 orders you have enough data to know: which products actually sell, what your real return rate is, which acquisition channel works for your brand, and what your unit economics look like at small scale. Everything before 100 is hypothesis. After 100, you're operating on evidence. Orders 1–10: Your Personal Network Your network Build relationships from the first introduction to the next order. Concept illustration Your first 10 orders should come from people who know you. Not because they're doing you a favor — but because getting them to pay full price validates that your positioning works. If people who like you won't pay for it, strangers definitely won't. Post on your personal Instagram and WhatsApp story with a real story behind the brand Message 50 people personally (not a broadcast) — explain the product, ask for their honest opinion Offer an early-supporter discount (15%) to the first 20 buyers — not a freebie, still paid Ask every buyer to share a photo with the product on their stories Orders 10–50: Community and WhatsApp Groups India has the world's most active WhatsApp group ecosystem. Local resident welfare groups, college alumni chats, professional networks, hobby groups — all of them are potential buyers for the right product. WhatsApp Group Outreach Don't post promotional messages directly. Instead, join relevant groups, contribute for 2–3 weeks, then share your product as "something I've been working on." The warm intro approach gets 10x the engagement of cold promotion. Orders 50–100: Instagram Organic and Influencer Seeding At 50 orders you have enough testimonials and product photos to build social proof. Use them to create Instagram content that answers questions your buyers had before purchasing. This becomes your content strategy. DM 50 micro-influencers (5K–50K followers) in your niche — offer free product, no paid contract Post 3 times per week: 1 product post, 1 behind-the-scenes, 1 customer story Use Instagram Stories daily — polls, questions, "swipe up" to your product Reply to every comment within 2 hours for the first 3 months Retain the First 100: The Thank You Advantage Keep customers Keep the conversation going before and after an order. Concept illustration Your first 100 buyers are your founding community. Treat them like it. A handwritten note in the package, a personal WhatsApp follow-up 5 days post-delivery, a referral incentive before they've moved on — these are low-cost actions with outsized loyalty returns. Post on your personal Instagram and WhatsApp story with a real story behind the brand Message 50 people personally (not a broadcast) — explain the product, ask for their honest opinion Offer an early-supporter discount (15%) to the first 20 buyers — not a freebie, still paid Ask every buyer to share a photo with the product on their stories Orders 10–50: Community and WhatsApp Groups India has the world's most active WhatsApp group ecosystem. Local resident welfare groups, college alumni chats, professional networks, hobby groups — all of them are potential buyers for the right product. WhatsApp Group Outreach Don't post promotional messages directly. Instead, join relevant groups, contribute for 2–3 weeks, then share your product as "something I've been working on." The warm intro approach gets 10x the engagement of cold promotion. Orders 50–100: Instagram Organic and Influencer Seeding At 50 orders you have enough testimonials and product photos to build social proof. Use them to create Instagram content that answers questions your buyers had before purchasing. This becomes your content strategy. DM 50 micro-influencers (5K–50K followers) in your niche — offer free product, no paid contract Post 3 times per week: 1 product post, 1 behind-the-scenes, 1 customer story Use Instagram Stories daily — polls, questions, "swipe up" to your product Reply to every comment within 2 hours for the first 3 months Retain the First 100: The Thank You Advantage Keep customers Keep the conversation going before and after an order. Concept illustration Your first 100 buyers are your founding community. Treat them like it. A handwritten note in the package, a personal WhatsApp follow-up 5 days post-delivery, a referral incentive before they've moved on — these are low-cost actions with outsized loyalty returns. R Ravi Krishnan Operations 12 Apr 2026 10 min read Updated 12 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # inventory # operations # warehouse # stock The guide, illustrated Understand what is in stock, where it belongs and what needs attention. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Prioritise stock 02 Reorder points 03 Locations ABC Analysis: Know Your Inventory Hierarchy Not all SKUs are equal. ABC analysis segments your inventory by revenue contribution: A-items (top 20% SKUs, 80% of revenue), B-items (30% SKUs, 15% revenue), C-items (50% SKUs, 5% revenue). Manage A-items obsessively, B-items systematically, and C-items lightly. Read this section Setting Reorder Points A reorder point is the stock level at which you automatically place a replenishment order. Formula: Reorder Point = (Average Daily Sales × Lead Time in Days) + Safety Stock. Read this section Multi-Location Inventory Once you're shipping more than 200 orders per day, consider splitting inventory between North (Delhi NCR), West (Mumbai), and South (Bengaluru/Hyderabad). Proximity to buyers reduces delivery time, cuts shipping costs, and improves customer experience. Read this section Running out of your bestseller during a sale event is the most expensive mistake in ecommerce operations. Overstocking a seasonal item is the second most expensive. Inventory management is the art of avoiding both. ABC Analysis: Know Your Inventory Hierarchy Prioritise stock Understand what is in stock, where it belongs and what needs attention. Concept illustration Not all SKUs are equal. ABC analysis segments your inventory by revenue contribution: A-items (top 20% SKUs, 80% of revenue), B-items (30% SKUs, 15% revenue), C-items (50% SKUs, 5% revenue). Manage A-items obsessively, B-items systematically, and C-items lightly. Setting Reorder Points A reorder point is the stock level at which you automatically place a replenishment order. Formula: Reorder Point = (Average Daily Sales × Lead Time in Days) + Safety Stock. Example You sell 20 units per day of a product. Your supplier takes 7 days to deliver. Safety stock = 3 days × 20 = 60 units. Reorder Point = (20 × 7) + 60 = 200 units. Order when you hit 200 units remaining. Safety Stock: Your Buffer Against Uncertainty Safety stock protects against demand spikes and supplier delays. For Indian supply chains — where courier delays and supplier stock-outs are common — maintain 3–7 days of safety stock for A-items. Dead Stock: The Hidden Cost Dead stock (inventory that hasn't moved in 90+ days) ties up capital and takes up warehouse space. Analyze your slow-movers quarterly and use bundles, discounts, or flash sales to liquidate. Better a ₹100 loss now than ₹500 in storage and eventual obsolescence. Multi-Location Inventory Locations Follow the work from available stock to a prepared parcel and delivery. Concept illustration Once you're shipping more than 200 orders per day, consider splitting inventory between North (Delhi NCR), West (Mumbai), and South (Bengaluru/Hyderabad). Proximity to buyers reduces delivery time, cuts shipping costs, and improves customer experience. LetBuyy supports multi-location inventory with per-warehouse stock tracking Set fulfillment priority rules (nearest warehouse to delivery address) Use separate reorder points per warehouse based on regional demand Track inter-warehouse transfers for full inventory visibility Article complete Up next: Order Fulfillment: Processing 100 Orders Per Day Efficiently 9 min read Continue learning R Ravi Krishnan Operations Supply chain and operations expert who has helped over 200 Indian brands streamline fulfillment and reduce return rates. 5 articles 1 topics Operations All articles by Ravi Weekly Newsletter Commerce guides and platform updates Commerce Insights Weekly AI Commerce insights India growth playbooks Platform feature updates Conversion rate tactics Email subscriptions are not available yet. P Priya Sharma Commerce Lead 10 May 2026 9 min read Updated 10 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # conversion # product-pages # ux # copywriting The guide, illustrated Show the product clearly, then help the buyer decide. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Photography 02 Product copy 03 Trust Photography: Your Most Important Asset In physical retail, customers pick products up. Online, photography does that work. Every product needs at minimum: a clean white background shot, 2–3 lifestyle shots showing the product in use, a close-up showing texture and quality, and a scale reference shot. Read this section Write Descriptions That Answer Questions, Not Just Describe Most product descriptions are written from a seller's perspective ("High-quality cotton kurta"). Buyers read from their own perspective ("Will this fabric breathe in Delhi summer?"). Rewrite every description as a set of answers to objections. Read this section Trust Signals That Matter for India Secure payment badge with UPI, Razorpay, and COD logos · GST invoice availability (critical for business buyers) Read this section The average Indian ecommerce product page converts at 1.5–2.5%. The top 10% of stores convert at 5–8%. The difference isn't traffic or advertising budget — it's the product page itself. The Anatomy of a High-Converting Product Page Before optimizing anything, understand what a buyer needs to answer before purchasing: Does this product solve my problem? Is the quality real? Can I trust this seller? What happens if I need to return it? Is the price fair? Photography: Your Most Important Asset Photography Show the product clearly, then help the buyer decide. Concept illustration In physical retail, customers pick products up. Online, photography does that work. Every product needs at minimum: a clean white background shot, 2–3 lifestyle shots showing the product in use, a close-up showing texture and quality, and a scale reference shot. Mobile-First Photography Over 78% of Indian ecommerce happens on mobile. Shoot your products in portrait orientation and test every image on a 360px wide screen. What looks great on desktop can look tiny on Redmi. Write Descriptions That Answer Questions, Not Just Describe Most product descriptions are written from a seller's perspective ("High-quality cotton kurta"). Buyers read from their own perspective ("Will this fabric breathe in Delhi summer?"). Rewrite every description as a set of answers to objections. Lead with the primary benefit (not a feature) Address the #1 objection in paragraph 2 List key specs in scannable bullet points End with a care/use instruction to reduce returns Add a single urgency signal if genuine (limited stock, sale ends) Reviews Are Your Best Sales Team Indian buyers are among the most review-reliant in the world. Products with 10+ reviews convert at 3x the rate of products with zero reviews. Your post-purchase flow should make leaving a review feel natural, not like a chore. Trust Signals That Matter for India Trust Build relationships from the first introduction to the next order. Concept illustration Secure payment badge with UPI, Razorpay, and COD logos GST invoice availability (critical for business buyers) 7-day or 14-day return policy displayed prominently WhatsApp support link for pre-purchase questions Real stock counts (creates urgency without fake pressure) Delivery estimate by PIN code The Price Anchoring Effect Show your MRP alongside your selling price when you can. Indian buyers are trained to look for discounts — a ₹999 product shown as "₹1,499 MRP, ₹999 today" converts significantly better than the same product shown as just ₹999, even if the economics are identical. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Technical SEO 02 Product pages 03 Content Technical SEO: The Foundation Core Web Vitals: LCP under 2.5s, FID under 100ms, CLS under 0.1 · Mobile-first: 78% of India's search happens on mobile Read this section On-Page SEO: Product Pages Unique title: [Product Name] — [Key Feature] | [Brand] · Meta description that includes price and a call to action Read this section Content SEO: Build a Resources Hub Transactional pages (product and category) rank for "buy" keywords. Content pages rank for "how to" and "what is" keywords — and they drive buyers at the consideration stage. A 2,000-word guide on "how to buy silk sarees online" will rank for hundreds of related queries and funnel readers toward your saree category. Read this section Paid ads are expensive and the moment you stop paying, traffic stops. SEO is slow and boring — and it's the only channel where traffic compounds over time. For Indian ecommerce, organic search is responsible for 35–45% of revenue for established brands. Technical SEO: The Foundation Technical SEO Connect the way people search with the products they can discover. Concept illustration Core Web Vitals: LCP under 2.5s, FID under 100ms, CLS under 0.1 Mobile-first: 78% of India's search happens on mobile HTTPS everywhere — no mixed content warnings Sitemap.xml submitted to Google Search Console Robots.txt configured correctly — no unintentional noindex Canonical tags on all paginated category pages Structured data: Product, BreadcrumbList, Organization India Speed Reality India's average mobile connection speed is 25 Mbps, but 40% of rural users are on 3G/4G. Your store must load usably in under 3 seconds on a Redmi device over a 3G connection. Test with Chrome's Network Throttling. On-Page SEO: Category Pages Category pages are your highest-volume SEO opportunity. A well-optimized "Cotton Kurtas for Women" category page can rank for thousands of related queries. Every category page needs: H1 with primary keyword, 150–200 word editorial description above the fold, and unique meta title and description. On-Page SEO: Product Pages Unique title: [Product Name] — [Key Feature] | [Brand] Meta description that includes price and a call to action H1 matches what people search, not your internal product name Alt text on every image with descriptive keywords Product schema with price, availability, and rating At least 300 words of unique description — no manufacturer copy Local and India-Specific SEO Signals Google India surfaces different results than Google global. Local signals that matter: Indian phone number in NAP data, .in TLD or India hosting signals, Hindi language pages for Tier 2 audiences, Google Business Profile for any physical presence, and regional payment method mentions (UPI, Paytm). Content SEO: Build a Resources Hub Content A few useful guides. A clearer path from learning to doing. Concept illustration Transactional pages (product and category) rank for "buy" keywords. Content pages rank for "how to" and "what is" keywords — and they drive buyers at the consideration stage. A 2,000-word guide on "how to buy silk sarees online" will rank for hundreds of related queries and funnel readers toward your saree category. L LetBuyy Team Platform 28 May 2026 11 min read Updated 16 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # getting-started # platform # store-setup # walkthrough The guide, illustrated Choose a theme, prepare your products, and bring your store to life. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Choose a theme 02 Add a product 03 Publish 3. Select a Theme Choose from free themes in the marketplace or upload a purchased theme. For your first store, start with "Clarity" (general merchandise) or "Urban" (fashion/lifestyle). Themes are fully customizable later. Read this section 4. Add Your First Product Navigate to Products → Add Product. Fill in: Title (what buyers search for), Description (what converts), Price (in INR), Compare-at Price (for discount display), Inventory quantity, and at least 3 product images. Read this section 8. Publish and Test Click "Publish Store" in your dashboard · Visit your store URL in an incognito window Read this section This is a literal click-by-click walkthrough of building a LetBuyy store from scratch. No prior experience needed. By the end, you'll have a published store ready to accept orders. 1. Create Your Account Go to accounts.letbuyy.com and sign up with your mobile number or Google account. Verify your phone number via OTP. You'll be taken directly to the store creation flow. 2. Name Your Store Choose your store name. This becomes your default URL (yourstore.letbuyy.com) and your brand name across the platform. You can add a custom domain later (Settings → Domains). Store Name Tips Keep it short (1–2 words), memorable, and relevant to what you sell. Avoid hyphens if possible. You can change your display name later but not your handle. 3. Select a Theme Choose a theme One design layer. A storefront that feels like you. Concept illustration Choose from free themes in the marketplace or upload a purchased theme. For your first store, start with "Clarity" (general merchandise) or "Urban" (fashion/lifestyle). Themes are fully customizable later. 4. Add Your First Product Navigate to Products → Add Product. Fill in: Title (what buyers search for), Description (what converts), Price (in INR), Compare-at Price (for discount display), Inventory quantity, and at least 3 product images. 5. Configure Payments Settings → Payments. Connect Razorpay with your API keys. Enable COD if appropriate for your category. Test with a ₹1 sandbox payment before going live. 6. Set Shipping Zones Settings → Shipping. Create zones: Local (same city, flat ₹40), State (same state, flat ₹60), National (all India, weight-based). Add a "Free shipping above ₹499" condition to each zone. 7. Enter Your GSTIN Settings → Business → GST. Enter your GSTIN to enable auto-invoice generation. Select your primary HSN codes for the product categories you sell. 8. Publish and Test Publish Follow the work from available stock to a prepared parcel and delivery. pages.text: How To Launch a D2C Brand in India (Step by Step) | LetBuyy Resources Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Resources All Ecommerce Growth Payments Operations AI Commerce Developers Changelog Commerce updates Contents 01 Phase 1: Find Your Niche (Weeks 1–2) 02 Phase 2: Build Your Brand Identity (Weeks 2–4) 03 Phase 3: Source and Package Your Product (Weeks 4–8) 04 Phase 4: Launch Strategy (Week 8) 05 Financial Targets for Your First Year 14 min read Updated Jun 2026 Share Print Back to Resources Resources › Growth How To Launch a D2C Brand in India (Step by Step) From idea to your first ₹1 lakh in revenue — the D2C playbook for Indian founders. P Priya Sharma Commerce Lead 10 Apr 2026 14 min read Updated 5 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # d2c # brand # launch # india The guide, illustrated Choose a theme, prepare your products, and bring your store to life. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Find your niche 02 Brand identity 03 Launch Phase 1: Find Your Niche (Weeks 1–2) The best Indian D2C brands in the last 5 years didn't try to be Mamaearth from day one. They started hyper-specific: only hair care for women with curly hair, only ghee sourced from Gir cows, only sneakers for people with wide feet. Read this section Phase 2: Build Your Brand Identity (Weeks 2–4) Your brand is not your logo. It's the answer to: "Why should I buy this from you instead of Amazon?" For Indian D2C, the most powerful answers are: made in India (regional pride), direct from the maker (authenticity), better quality for less (value), or cause-driven (sustainability, artisan support). Read this section Phase 4: Launch Strategy (Week 8) Your launch is not a one-day event. It's a 30-day campaign with three stages: teaser (build anticipation), launch (drive first purchases), and amplification (turn buyers into advocates). Read this section India minted over 200 new D2C brands every month in 2025. The ones that survive share one trait: they went deep on a specific customer before going broad on the market. This guide shows you how. Phase 1: Find Your Niche (Weeks 1–2) Find your niche One design layer. A storefront that feels like you. Concept illustration The best Indian D2C brands in the last 5 years didn't try to be Mamaearth from day one. They started hyper-specific: only hair care for women with curly hair, only ghee sourced from Gir cows, only sneakers for people with wide feet. India Niche Opportunity India's middle class is 400 million people. A 0.1% niche is 400,000 potential buyers — enough to build a ₹10+ crore brand with no external funding. Phase 2: Build Your Brand Identity (Weeks 2–4) Your brand is not your logo. It's the answer to: "Why should I buy this from you instead of Amazon?" For Indian D2C, the most powerful answers are: made in India (regional pride), direct from the maker (authenticity), better quality for less (value), or cause-driven (sustainability, artisan support). Phase 3: Source and Package Your Product (Weeks 4–8) India has world-class manufacturing in textiles, ceramics, leather, pharma ingredients, and agricultural products — most of it underbranded. Your product sourcing strategy and packaging quality will determine your perceived value ceiling. Offer COD at All Tiers 2. Show Final Price Before Checkout 3. WhatsApp Cart Recovery 4. Simplify the Checkout to 2 Steps 5. Guest Checkout Always 6. Add PIN Code Delivery Estimate on Cart Page 7. Show Micro Social Proof at Checkout 8. Sticky Exit Intent on Mobile 8 min read Updated Jun 2026 Share Print Back to Resources Resources › Ecommerce Reducing Cart Abandonment: 12 Proven Strategies for Indian Stores 70% of Indian shoppers abandon their cart. Here's how to get them back. P Priya Sharma Commerce Lead 22 Apr 2026 8 min read Updated 1 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # conversion # cart # recovery # whatsapp The guide, illustrated Two payment paths, one customer journey: pay digitally or pay on delivery. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Find the friction 02 Recover carts Understand Why Indian Buyers Abandon No COD option available (top reason in Tier 2/3) · Unexpected shipping charges at checkout Read this section The 12 Strategies Enable COD for every order under ₹5,000 without prepayment requirements. The return risk is real but the revenue unlock is bigger. You can manage RTO with stricter PIN code filtering and NDR automation. Read this section India has one of the highest cart abandonment rates in the world — around 70–75% globally, but crossing 80% for some Indian categories. COD hesitation, slow loading on 4G, and trust gaps at checkout are the three biggest drivers. Understand Why Indian Buyers Abandon Find the friction Two payment paths, one customer journey: pay digitally or pay on delivery. Concept illustration No COD option available (top reason in Tier 2/3) Unexpected shipping charges at checkout Page loaded too slowly on mobile No WhatsApp or phone support for last-minute questions Forced account creation before purchase UPI app switch friction on mobile browsers The 12 Strategies Recover carts Keep the conversation going before and after an order. Concept illustration 1. Offer COD at All Tiers Enable COD for every order under ₹5,000 without prepayment requirements. The return risk is real but the revenue unlock is bigger. You can manage RTO with stricter PIN code filtering and NDR automation. 2. Show Final Price Before Checkout Display estimated shipping costs on the product page or cart — not as a surprise at checkout. "Free shipping above ₹499" shown early converts better than the same offer revealed at checkout. 3. WhatsApp Cart Recovery India's WhatsApp open rate is 98%. A personalized WhatsApp message — "Hey Rohan, you left something behind" with a product image — sent 2 hours after abandonment recovers 8–12% of abandoned carts. 4. Simplify the Checkout to 2 Steps Every additional form field drops conversion by ~10%. Collect only what you need: name, phone (not email — they'll share phone), delivery address, and payment. Don't ask for date of birth, gender, or alternate email at checkout. 5. Guest Checkout Always Never force account creation before a first purchase. Offer to "save your details" after the order is confirmed — that's when trust is highest and consent feels natural. LetBuyy Checkout LetBuyy's checkout is pre-optimized for Indian payment flows: UPI deeplinks, COD with PIN verification, saved addresses via phone number, and no forced account creation. 6. Add PIN Code Delivery Estimate on Cart Page "Estimated delivery: 3–5 business days" is vague. "Estimated delivery to 400001: Tuesday, June 24" with a live PIN code checker is concrete — and converts. 7. Show Micro Social Proof at Checkout "₹2.3 crore worth of orders shipped" or "47 people bought this in the last 24 hours" at the checkout page reduces anxiety at the most vulnerable point in the funnel. 8. Sticky Exit Intent on Mobile When a mobile user scrolls up (classic exit signal), show a sticky bottom bar: "Wait — your order qualifies for free shipping. Complete it now." Keep it dismissible and non-intrusive. P Priya Sharma Commerce Lead 1 Apr 2026 7 min read Updated 20 May 2026 Copy link Save # reviews # social-proof # conversion # trust The guide, illustrated Build relationships from the first introduction to the next order. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Build trust 02 Collect reviews 03 Respond Why Indian Buyers Trust Reviews More Than Ads India has a strong word-of-mouth culture. Before ecommerce, buying decisions were made at the recommendation of neighbors, family, or trusted shopkeepers. Reviews are digital word-of-mouth — and they carry disproportionate weight in categories like fashion, electronics, and cosmetics. Read this section The Review Collection Playbook Send a WhatsApp message 5 days after delivery: "How is your [product]? Reply with your rating (1–5)" — WhatsApp reviews get 3x the response rate of email · Follow up with email at day 8 with a photo review request and a small incentive (10% off next order) Read this section Handling Negative Reviews A product with all 5-star reviews looks fake. A product with a 4.2 average and a thoughtful response to every 3-star review looks real. Respond to every critical review within 24 hours. Offer to resolve offline. Update your response when resolved. Read this section A product with 50 reviews converts at 4.6% on average. A product with zero reviews converts at 1.7%. That's a 270% lift — from nothing but social proof. And the gap widens as Indian buyers become more sophisticated and review-dependent. Why Indian Buyers Trust Reviews More Than Ads Build trust Build relationships from the first introduction to the next order. Concept illustration India has a strong word-of-mouth culture. Before ecommerce, buying decisions were made at the recommendation of neighbors, family, or trusted shopkeepers. Reviews are digital word-of-mouth — and they carry disproportionate weight in categories like fashion, electronics, and cosmetics. The Review Collection Playbook Send a WhatsApp message 5 days after delivery: "How is your [product]? Reply with your rating (1–5)" — WhatsApp reviews get 3x the response rate of email Follow up with email at day 8 with a photo review request and a small incentive (10% off next order) Add a QR code inside your packaging linking to the review page Respond to every review publicly — shows buyers you're engaged Feature top reviews in your product images as overlays Never Buy Fake Reviews Fake reviews erode trust when discovered — and buyers are increasingly sophisticated at spotting them. A single credible bad review responded to well is worth more than ten suspicious 5-star reviews. Display Strategy: Show Reviews Where They Convert Don't just put reviews at the bottom of the page. Surface star ratings near the price, show 2–3 top reviews immediately under the add-to-cart button, and display review counts in search results via structured data. Handling Negative Reviews Respond Keep the conversation going before and after an order. Concept illustration A product with all 5-star reviews looks fake. A product with a 4.2 average and a thoughtful response to every 3-star review looks real. Respond to every critical review within 24 hours. Offer to resolve offline. Update your response when resolved. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 The basics 02 Monthly filing 03 Input credit GST Basics for Ecommerce GST (Goods and Services Tax) replaced 17 central and state taxes in 2017. For ecommerce, the key principle is: GST is charged at the point of supply (where goods are delivered), collected from the buyer, and remitted to the government monthly. Read this section Monthly Filing: GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B GSTR-1: File by 11th of every month — list all outward supplies (sales) · GSTR-3B: File by 20th of every month — net tax liability after input credit Read this section Input Tax Credit: Your Cost Advantage Input Tax Credit (ITC) lets you deduct GST paid on business purchases from GST collected on sales. If you pay ₹18 GST on packaging materials and collect ₹60 GST on sales, you only remit ₹42. This is significant — ITC on packaging, courier services, and raw materials can reduce your effective tax rate by 30–40%. Read this section GST is the one compliance task that stops more Indian brands from scaling than any other. The fear is understandable — GST has its own terminology, its own portal, and its own filing schedule. But once you understand the fundamentals, it becomes a system, not a burden. GST Basics for Ecommerce The basics Keep sales, invoices and the supporting records connected. Concept illustration GST (Goods and Services Tax) replaced 17 central and state taxes in 2017. For ecommerce, the key principle is: GST is charged at the point of supply (where goods are delivered), collected from the buyer, and remitted to the government monthly. Do You Need GST Registration? Annual turnover above ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh in special category states): Mandatory Annual turnover below ₹20 lakh: Optional but recommended for input tax credit Selling on marketplaces (Amazon, Flipkart): Mandatory regardless of turnover Selling via your own website to other states: Mandatory regardless of turnover Marketplace TCS Marketplaces like Amazon and Flipkart are required to collect Tax Collected at Source (TCS) at 1% of your taxable sales and deposit it with the government. This appears in your GSTR-2A and must be reconciled. GST Rates for Common Ecommerce Categories Category GST Rate Notes Apparel below ₹1,000 5% Reduced rate for affordable clothing Apparel above ₹1,000 12% Footwear below ₹1,000 5% Electronics 18% Most consumer electronics Packaged food (branded) 12% FSSAI registered products Beauty and personal care 18% Most categories Books 0% Exempt Handloomed textiles 5% Special rate Monthly Filing: GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B GSTR-1: File by 11th of every month — list all outward supplies (sales) GSTR-3B: File by 20th of every month — net tax liability after input credit Pay any tax due by the GSTR-3B filing date Reconcile TCS in GSTR-2A before filing GSTR-3B Input Tax Credit: Your Cost Advantage Input credit Understand what is in stock, where it belongs and what needs attention. Concept illustration Input Tax Credit (ITC) lets you deduct GST paid on business purchases from GST collected on sales. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Connect 02 Configure COD 03 Enable UPI Step 2: Connect Razorpay to LetBuyy Go to Settings → Payments in your Merchant Control Plane · Click "Connect Razorpay" and enter your API key and secret Read this section Step 3: Configure COD COD on LetBuyy is configured per PIN code zone. You can enable COD globally and block specific PIN codes with high RTO, or restrict COD to specific states. Set a minimum order value (recommended: ₹299) and maximum (recommended: ₹5,000). Read this section Step 4: Enable UPI UPI is automatically enabled when Razorpay is connected. LetBuyy's checkout renders UPI intent links for mobile browsers, reducing the UPI friction by eliminating manual VPA entry. Read this section LetBuyy's payment system is built for India from the ground up — UPI, COD, Razorpay, EMI, and wallet support are all native, not third-party plugins. Here's how to configure everything. Step 1: Create Your Razorpay Account LetBuyy uses Razorpay as the primary payment processor for card, UPI, netbanking, and EMI. You'll need a Razorpay business account with KYC completed. The KYC process takes 1–3 business days and requires your PAN, bank statement, and GSTIN. Step 2: Connect Razorpay to LetBuyy Connect Connect requests, events and access to the work your store needs. Concept illustration Go to Settings → Payments in your Merchant Control Plane Click "Connect Razorpay" and enter your API key and secret Enable webhook verification in your Razorpay dashboard Test a payment of ₹1 in sandbox mode Switch to live mode after verification Webhook Security LetBuyy verifies Razorpay webhook signatures using HMAC-SHA256. Never disable webhook verification — it's your protection against fraudulent payment confirmation. Step 3: Configure COD COD on LetBuyy is configured per PIN code zone. You can enable COD globally and block specific PIN codes with high RTO, or restrict COD to specific states. Set a minimum order value (recommended: ₹299) and maximum (recommended: ₹5,000). Step 4: Enable UPI Enable UPI Two payment paths, one customer journey: pay digitally or pay on delivery. Concept illustration UPI is automatically enabled when Razorpay is connected. LetBuyy's checkout renders UPI intent links for mobile browsers, reducing the UPI friction by eliminating manual VPA entry. pages.text: Building a Customer-Friendly Returns Policy for India | LetBuyy Resources Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Resources All Ecommerce Growth Payments Operations AI Commerce Developers Changelog Commerce updates Contents 01 What Indian Buyers Expect 02 Writing Your Policy 03 Managing Return Costs 8 min read Updated May 2026 Share Print Back to Resources Resources › Payments Building a Customer-Friendly Returns Policy for India The right returns policy builds trust and reduces RTO — without killing your margins. N Neha Gupta Payments & Compliance 20 Mar 2026 8 min read Updated 30 May 2026 Copy link Save # returns # refunds # policy # customer-service The guide, illustrated Make the return journey as clear as the purchase. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Expectations 02 Your policy 03 Return costs What Indian Buyers Expect 7–14 day return window (14 days is competitive advantage) · Free return pickup for damaged or wrong items Read this section Writing Your Policy Write your policy in plain Hindi and English. Avoid legal jargon. Use simple language: "If you don't love it, here's how to send it back." Include: what is eligible for return, what isn't, how to initiate a return, the timeline, and how the refund is issued. Read this section Managing Return Costs Charge a small handling fee (₹50–100) for non-defective returns · Require photo evidence for damage claims before approving pickup Read this section Indian buyers check the returns policy before buying. Brands with clear, fair return policies convert at 20% higher rates than those with restrictive or unclear policies. But a policy that's too liberal can destroy margins. What Indian Buyers Expect Expectations Keep the conversation going before and after an order. Concept illustration 7–14 day return window (14 days is competitive advantage) Free return pickup for damaged or wrong items Exchange option, not just refund Refund timeline clearly stated (7–10 working days) No questions asked for size issues in fashion Writing Your Policy Write your policy in plain Hindi and English. Avoid legal jargon. Use simple language: "If you don't love it, here's how to send it back." Include: what is eligible for return, what isn't, how to initiate a return, the timeline, and how the refund is issued. Managing Return Costs Return costs Make the return journey as clear as the purchase. Concept illustration Charge a small handling fee (₹50–100) for non-defective returns Require photo evidence for damage claims before approving pickup Offer store credit at 110% value as alternative to refund Block serial returners from COD (high correlation with RTO) Quality Photography Reduces Returns Most fashion returns happen because the product looks different in person than in the photos. Accurate color representation and scale shots reduce fashion return rates by 15–20%. R Ravi Krishnan Operations 28 Apr 2026 11 min read Updated 14 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # shipping # logistics # courier # india The guide, illustrated Follow the work from available stock to a prepared parcel and delivery. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Couriers 02 Parcel weight 03 Tracking Courier Comparison Explore the examples and explanation in this section. Read this section Weight Slabs and Volumetric Weight Most couriers bill whichever is higher: actual weight or volumetric weight (L×B×H/5000 in cm). A lightweight product in a large box can be billed at 2–3x its actual weight. Optimize your packaging dimensions to minimize this. Read this section Tracking and NDR Automation Non-Delivery Reports (NDR) occur when a delivery attempt fails. Without follow-up, NDRs become RTOs (return to origin) — you've paid shipping both ways with zero revenue. Automate NDR follow-up: WhatsApp message within 2 hours of failed delivery, offering to reschedule. Read this section India has 19,101 PIN codes. Your ability to serve them determines your total addressable market. Most Indian brands start with 3,000–5,000 PIN codes through a single courier, leaving 60–70% of the country unserved. Courier Comparison Couriers Follow the work from available stock to a prepared parcel and delivery. Concept illustration Courier PIN Coverage Transit Time COD Support Best For Delhivery 18,000+ 3–5 days ✓ Volume sellers BlueDart 35,000+ 2–3 days ✓ Premium, time-sensitive Shiprocket 26,000+ (aggregator) 3–6 days ✓ Small sellers (<500/month) DTDC 10,000+ 4–7 days ✓ Widest Tier 4 coverage Xpressbees 15,000+ 3–5 days ✓ Competitive rates Rate Negotiation Shipping rates are negotiable — don't accept list prices. At 100 shipments/month, you can negotiate 5–10% off. At 1,000/month, 15–25%. At 5,000/month, 30–40%. Get quotes from 3 couriers simultaneously and use competing offers as leverage. Weight Slabs and Volumetric Weight Volumetric Weight Billing Most couriers bill whichever is higher: actual weight or volumetric weight (L×B×H/5000 in cm). A lightweight product in a large box can be billed at 2–3x its actual weight. Optimize your packaging dimensions to minimize this. Tracking and NDR Automation Tracking Make the return journey as clear as the purchase. Concept illustration Non-Delivery Reports (NDR) occur when a delivery attempt fails. Without follow-up, NDRs become RTOs (return to origin) — you've paid shipping both ways with zero revenue. Automate NDR follow-up: WhatsApp message within 2 hours of failed delivery, offering to reschedule. pages.text: Multi-Warehouse Inventory Management | LetBuyy Resources Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Resources All Ecommerce Growth Payments Operations AI Commerce Developers Changelog Commerce updates Contents 01 When to Go Multi-Warehouse 02 Zone Strategy for India 03 Stock Allocation by Zone 04 Inter-Warehouse Transfers 8 min read Updated Jun 2026 Share Print Back to Resources Resources › Operations Multi-Warehouse Inventory Management Distribute stock closer to your buyers and cut delivery times by 60%. R Ravi Krishnan Operations 20 May 2026 8 min read Updated 16 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # inventory # warehouse # multi-location # operations The guide, illustrated Understand what is in stock, where it belongs and what needs attention. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 When to expand 02 Allocate stock 03 Transfers When to Go Multi-Warehouse More than 200 daily orders · Significant sales from more than one region Read this section Stock Allocation by Zone Analyze 90 days of orders by delivery state. Allocate stock proportionally: if 35% of orders go to North, keep 35% of A-item inventory there. Rebalance quarterly based on actual sales data. Read this section Inter-Warehouse Transfers When one zone runs low, transfer from another. Track inter-warehouse transfers as inventory movements — not sales — to keep your stock counts accurate. LetBuyy generates transfer orders and updates both warehouse inventories in real time. Read this section Selling from a single warehouse in Delhi means a buyer in Chennai waits 5–7 days. Storing 20% of your inventory in Bengaluru cuts that to 2 days. Multi-warehouse is the highest-impact operations upgrade for brands above ₹50 lakh annual revenue. When to Go Multi-Warehouse When to expand Understand what is in stock, where it belongs and what needs attention. Concept illustration More than 200 daily orders Significant sales from more than one region Average transit time above 4 days to major cities Shipping costs above 8% of revenue Zone Strategy for India India's logistics network divides naturally into 4 zones. Start with 2 warehouses (North + South), then add West. North warehouse serves Delhi, UP, Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab. South serves Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra, Kerala. West serves Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa. Stock Allocation by Zone Analyze 90 days of orders by delivery state. Allocate stock proportionally: if 35% of orders go to North, keep 35% of A-item inventory there. Rebalance quarterly based on actual sales data. LetBuyy Multi-Location LetBuyy's inventory module supports unlimited warehouse locations. Fulfillment routing automatically picks the nearest warehouse to the delivery address, with fallback to next-nearest if out of stock. Inter-Warehouse Transfers Transfers Follow the work from available stock to a prepared parcel and delivery. Concept illustration When one zone runs low, transfer from another. Track inter-warehouse transfers as inventory movements — not sales — to keep your stock counts accurate. LetBuyy generates transfer orders and updates both warehouse inventories in real time.
