pages.text: Understanding Ecommerce Fulfillment in India | LetBuyy Resources Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Resources All Ecommerce Growth Payments Operations AI Commerce Developers Changelog Commerce updates Contents 01 Model 1: Self-Fulfillment (0–500 orders/month) 02 Model 2: Third-Party Logistics / 3PL (200–5,000 orders/month) 03 Choosing a 3PL Partner 9 min read Updated May 2026 Share Print Back to Resources Resources › Operations Understanding Ecommerce Fulfillment in India Self-fulfillment, 3PL, or marketplace fulfillment — which is right for your brand? R Ravi Krishnan Operations 10 Mar 2026 9 min read Updated 25 May 2026 Copy link Save # fulfillment # 3pl # logistics # operations The guide, illustrated Follow the work from available stock to a prepared parcel and delivery. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Self-fulfillment 02 Logistics partner 03 Choose a partner Model 1: Self-Fulfillment (0–500 orders/month) You pack and ship from your own space — home, office, or rented warehouse. Lowest cost, most control over brand experience. Ceiling: typically 500 orders/month before it consumes too much founder time. Read this section Model 2: Third-Party Logistics / 3PL (200–5,000 orders/month) A 3PL warehouses your inventory, picks, packs, and ships on your behalf. You integrate with their system, send a PO when stock is low, and pay per-order fulfillment fees. Indian 3PLs include Shiprocket Fulfillment, WareIQ, and Loadshare. Read this section Choosing a 3PL Partner Minimum monthly volume requirement (some require 500+ orders) · Per-pick and per-pack fees (compare total cost per order) Read this section How you fulfill orders affects your delivery time, your cost structure, your brand experience, and how much time you spend on operations vs. growth. The right model depends on your volume, your product type, and your growth stage. Model 1: Self-Fulfillment (0–500 orders/month) Self-fulfillment Follow the work from available stock to a prepared parcel and delivery. Concept illustration You pack and ship from your own space — home, office, or rented warehouse. Lowest cost, most control over brand experience. Ceiling: typically 500 orders/month before it consumes too much founder time. Model 2: Third-Party Logistics / 3PL (200–5,000 orders/month) A 3PL warehouses your inventory, picks, packs, and ships on your behalf. You integrate with their system, send a PO when stock is low, and pay per-order fulfillment fees. Indian 3PLs include Shiprocket Fulfillment, WareIQ, and Loadshare. Model Cost per Order Control Scalability Best For Self-Fulfill ₹0 labor + courier High Limited <500 orders/month 3PL ₹30–80 + courier Medium High 200–10,000/month FBA/FBF ₹50–150 + courier Low Very High Marketplace-first brands Choosing a 3PL Partner Choose a partner Understand what is in stock, where it belongs and what needs attention. Concept illustration Minimum monthly volume requirement (some require 500+ orders) Per-pick and per-pack fees (compare total cost per order) WMS (Warehouse Management System) quality — can it integrate with LetBuyy? Returns handling capability and cost Locations — do they have warehouses in your target zones? Hybrid Model The best-performing Indian brands use a hybrid: self-fulfill in your home region (where you have most control) and 3PL in remote zones (where you have poor logistics). This minimizes cost while maximizing reach. Model 2: Third-Party Logistics / 3PL (200–5,000 orders/month) A 3PL warehouses your inventory, picks, packs, and ships on your behalf. You integrate with their system, send a PO when stock is low, and pay per-order fulfillment fees. Indian 3PLs include Shiprocket Fulfillment, WareIQ, and Loadshare. Model Cost per Order Control Scalability Best For Self-Fulfill ₹0 labor + courier High Limited <500 orders/month 3PL ₹30–80 + courier Medium High 200–10,000/month FBA/FBF ₹50–150 + courier Low Very High Marketplace-first brands Choosing a 3PL Partner Choose a partner Understand what is in stock, where it belongs and what needs attention. Concept illustration Minimum monthly volume requirement (some require 500+ orders) Per-pick and per-pack fees (compare total cost per order) WMS (Warehouse Management System) quality — can it integrate with LetBuyy? Returns handling capability and cost Locations — do they have warehouses in your target zones? Hybrid Model The best-performing Indian brands use a hybrid: self-fulfill in your home region (where you have most control) and 3PL in remote zones (where you have poor logistics). This minimizes cost while maximizing reach. pages.text:
Building Your First LetBuyy App | LetBuyy Resources Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Resources All Ecommerce Growth Payments Operations AI Commerce Developers Changelog Commerce updates Contents 01 App Types 02 Step 1: Register Your App 03 Step 2: Implement OAuth 2.0 04 Step 3: Embed Your UI 05 Step 4: Submit to the Marketplace 13 min read Updated Jun 2026 Share Print Back to Resources Resources › Developers Building Your First LetBuyy App From OAuth to your first embedded app in the Merchant Control Plane. A Arjun Mehta Developer Relations 22 May 2026 13 min read Updated 15 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # apps # oauth # developers # marketplace The guide, illustrated A connected view of shipping, marketing, analytics, operations, and support. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 App types 02 Authorise 03 Embed App Types Public Apps: Listed in the App Marketplace, installable by any merchant · Private Apps: Created for a single store, not listed publicly Read this section Step 2: Implement OAuth 2.0 Store access_token and refresh_token encrypted at rest. Never log them. Rotate refresh tokens on every use. Token exposure = full store access for the attacker. Read this section Step 3: Embed Your UI LetBuyy's App Bridge lets you render your app UI inside the Merchant Control Plane. Your app loads in an iframe, and App Bridge provides authenticated communication between your app and the MCP host. Read this section A LetBuyy App is a web application that merchants install from the App Marketplace. It gets access to store data via OAuth 2.0, can embed a UI inside the Merchant Control Plane, and can listen to events via webhooks. App Types App types A connected view of shipping, marketing, analytics, operations, and support. Concept illustration Public Apps: Listed in the App Marketplace, installable by any merchant Private Apps: Created for a single store, not listed publicly Custom Apps: Built for a specific merchant group (e.g. a 3PL) with restricted access Step 1: Register Your App Create an app in the LetBuyy Developer Portal. You'll get a Client ID and Client Secret. Set your OAuth callback URL — this must be HTTPS in production. Step 2: Implement OAuth 2.0 // Step 1: Redirect to LetBuyy OAuth
const authUrl = `https://accounts.letbuyy.com/oauth/authorize?
  client_id=${CLIENT_ID}&
  redirect_uri=${REDIRECT_URI}&
  scope=orders:read products:write&
  state=${generateState()}`

// Step 2: Exchange code for tokens

Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Dashboard 02 Products 03 Orders Dashboard: Your Daily Command Center The dashboard opens on today's key metrics: revenue, orders, conversion rate, and average order value. Below the metrics, you'll see: pending orders requiring action, low stock alerts, recent customer messages, and your AI Copilot feed. Read this section Products Module Products: Create, edit, organize, and bulk-update your catalog · Collections: Group products by category, season, or campaign Read this section Orders Module All Orders: View, filter, and process all orders · Fulfillment Queue: Prioritized list of orders to pick, pack, and ship Read this section The Merchant Control Plane (MCP) is your commerce headquarters. Dashboard: Your Daily Command Center Dashboard A connected view of shipping, marketing, analytics, operations, and support. Concept illustration The dashboard opens on today's key metrics: revenue, orders, conversion rate, and average order value. Below the metrics, you'll see: pending orders requiring action, low stock alerts, recent customer messages, and your AI Copilot feed. Products Module Products: Create, edit, organize, and bulk-update your catalog Collections: Group products by category, season, or campaign Inventory: Track stock levels across all locations Purchase Orders: Create and track supplier orders Orders Module Orders Follow the work from available stock to a prepared parcel and delivery. Concept illustration All Orders: View, filter, and process all orders Fulfillment Queue: Prioritized list of orders to pick, pack, and ship Returns: Process and track return requests COD Orders: Manage cash collection and confirmation Customers Module Search customers by name, phone, or email. View their full purchase history, LTV, and average order value. Tag customers for segmentation (loyalty tier, city, acquisition channel). Export for WhatsApp or email campaigns. Analytics Module Revenue: Daily, weekly, monthly trends with year-over-year comparison Products: Best sellers, slow movers, and margin analysis Customers: New vs. returning, geographic distribution, acquisition sources Conversion: Funnel analysis from landing to purchase Keyboard Shortcut Press Cmd+K (Mac) or Ctrl+K (Windows) anywhere in the MCP to open the AI Copilot. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Store context 02 Useful prompts 03 Daily work What the Copilot Knows All your products, prices, variants, and inventory levels · Your last 90 days of orders and customer data Read this section Useful Prompts for Merchants The Copilot can read your store data and generate content, but it cannot make changes without your confirmation. All suggestions require your explicit approval before anything is updated. Read this section Copilot Across the Merchant Control Plane The Copilot is context-aware: in Products, it offers writing and SEO help. In Orders, it surfaces insights and alerts. In Inventory, it predicts reorders. In Customers, it suggests segments. The same AI assistant adapts to where you are. Read this section The LetBuyy AI Copilot is always available in your merchant dashboard — top-right corner, or press Cmd+K. It has full context about your store: products, orders, customers, inventory, and settings. Ask it anything. What the Copilot Knows Store context A useful conversation starts with the context of your business. Concept illustration All your products, prices, variants, and inventory levels Your last 90 days of orders and customer data Your shipping zones, payment configuration, and store settings Your store's performance metrics (revenue, conversion, AOV) LetBuyy platform documentation and best practices Useful Prompts for Merchants Product Content "Write a product description for my "Organic Cotton Kurta" product that emphasizes fabric quality, fits for the Indian summer, and answers sizing concerns. Include care instructions." Operations "Which of my products are likely to stockout in the next 14 days based on current sales velocity? List them with urgency ranking." Customer Insights "Who are my top 20 customers by lifetime value? What products do they share in common?" Marketing "Write 5 Instagram captions for my Summer Collection launch, targeting young women in Indian metros. Include relevant hashtags." Copilot Limits The Copilot can read your store data and generate content, but it cannot make changes without your confirmation. All suggestions require your explicit approval before anything is updated. L LetBuyy Team Platform 30 May 2026 8 min read Updated 16 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # platform # overview # architecture # product The guide, illustrated A connected view of shipping, marketing, analytics, operations, and support. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Core surfaces 02 Connections 03 India-first The Core Surfaces Merchant Control Plane (merchant.letbuyy.com): Where you run your store — products, orders, customers, inventory, analytics, settings · Storefront Runtime ({store}.letbuyy.com): Your live store, powered by your theme and products Read this section The Architecture in Plain Language Every LetBuyy store is identified by a site_id. All data (products, orders, customers, inventory) is scoped to your site_id. When a buyer visits your store, the storefront runtime uses your site_id to look up your configuration, theme, and products. When a merchant logs in, their session is scoped to the store(s) they own. Read this section India-First Decisions in the Platform Money is stored as minor units (paise) to avoid floating-point errors · GST invoices are generated automatically for every order Read this section LetBuyy is not a website builder. It's a commerce operating system — a connected set of surfaces that merchants, developers, operators, and customers interact with simultaneously. The Core Surfaces Core surfaces A connected view of shipping, marketing, analytics, operations, and support. Concept illustration Merchant Control Plane (merchant.letbuyy.com): Where you run your store — products, orders, customers, inventory, analytics, settings Storefront Runtime ({store}.letbuyy.com): Your live store, powered by your theme and products Identity Platform (accounts.letbuyy.com): Authentication, onboarding, plan management App Marketplace (apps.letbuyy.com): Install third-party extensions Theme Marketplace (themes.letbuyy.com): Browse and purchase themes Developer Portal (developer.letbuyy.com): API docs, webhook management, app creation The Architecture in Plain Language Every LetBuyy store is identified by a site_id. All data (products, orders, customers, inventory) is scoped to your site_id. When a buyer visits your store, the storefront runtime uses your site_id to look up your configuration, theme, and products. When a merchant logs in, their session is scoped to the store(s) they own. India-First Decisions in the Platform India-first Two payment paths, one customer journey: pay digitally or pay on delivery. pages.text: Customer Retention Strategies That Work for Indian Brands | LetBuyy Resources Why LetBuyy Products Themes Apps Developers Pricing Log in Start for free Start for free Resources All Ecommerce Growth Payments Operations AI Commerce Developers Changelog Commerce updates Contents 01 The Retention Funnel: Three Stages 02 Loyalty Programs That Actually Work in India 03 Re-engagement: Winning Back Lapsed Buyers 04 The Referral Engine 8 min read Updated Jun 2026 Share Print Back to Resources Resources › Growth Customer Retention Strategies That Work for Indian Brands Acquiring a new customer costs 5x more than retaining one. Here's how to keep them. P Priya Sharma Commerce Lead 5 May 2026 8 min read Updated 10 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # retention # loyalty # ltv # repeat-purchase The guide, illustrated Keep the conversation going before and after an order. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Retention 02 Loyalty 03 Re-engagement The Retention Funnel: Three Stages Retention isn't a single action — it's a funnel: Activation (did the customer have a great first experience?), Habit formation (did they buy again within 90 days?), Advocacy (did they refer someone?). Read this section Loyalty Programs That Actually Work in India Points programs work when the reward is tangible and the earning is simple. The fatal mistake: making points worth ₹0.01 each so a buyer needs 100 orders to earn anything meaningful. Set your redemption rate so a typical order earns something usable in 2–3 purchases. Read this section Re-engagement: Winning Back Lapsed Buyers Identify customers who haven't purchased in 90+ days · Send a "We miss you" WhatsApp with a personalized discount (15%) Read this section The top 20% of customers account for 80% of revenue for most Indian ecommerce brands. Yet most brands spend 90% of their marketing budget trying to acquire the other 80%. Flipping this ratio is the single highest-leverage growth move available. The Retention Funnel: Three Stages Retention Build relationships from the first introduction to the next order. Concept illustration Retention isn't a single action — it's a funnel: Activation (did the customer have a great first experience?), Habit formation (did they buy again within 90 days?), Advocacy (did they refer someone?). Loyalty Programs That Actually Work in India Points programs work when the reward is tangible and the earning is simple. The fatal mistake: making points worth ₹0.01 each so a buyer needs 100 orders to earn anything meaningful. Set your redemption rate so a typical order earns something usable in 2–3 purchases. Re-engagement: Winning Back Lapsed Buyers Re-engagement Keep the conversation going before and after an order. Concept illustration Identify customers who haven't purchased in 90+ days Send a "We miss you" WhatsApp with a personalized discount (15%) Follow up with email showing new products since their last purchase Final effort: "Your discount expires in 48 hours" — creates urgency The 90-Day Window Research across Indian D2C brands shows that customers who don't buy again within 90 days of their first purchase have a 75% churn probability. Your re-engagement window is tight — act early. The Referral Engine India's referral conversion rate is 30% higher than Western markets because of strong word-of-mouth culture. A simple "give ₹100, get ₹100" referral program, promoted at the right moment (post-delivery, when satisfaction is highest), can generate 20–30% of new revenue for mature brands. L LetBuyy Team Platform 30 Apr 2026 7 min read Updated 10 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # recommendations # ai # conversion # personalization The guide, illustrated Help buyers discover products that make sense together. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 How it works 02 Types 03 Placement How Recommendations Work LetBuyy's recommendation engine uses collaborative filtering: "buyers who bought this product also bought these products." With enough order data (typically 500+ orders), the recommendations become accurate and personalized. Read this section Types of Recommendations "You may also like" — products similar to what's being viewed (product page) · "Complete the look" — complementary products (fashion, home decor) Read this section Placement Strategy Place recommendations at high-intent moments: below the add-to-cart button (highest converting placement), in the cart before checkout, in the post-purchase confirmation email, and on the homepage for returning visitors. Read this section Product recommendations drive 35% of Amazon's revenue. The same intelligence is now available to independent Indian stores through LetBuyy's recommendation engine — no ML team required. How Recommendations Work How it works Help buyers discover products that make sense together. Concept illustration LetBuyy's recommendation engine uses collaborative filtering: "buyers who bought this product also bought these products." With enough order data (typically 500+ orders), the recommendations become accurate and personalized. Types of Recommendations "You may also like" — products similar to what's being viewed (product page) "Complete the look" — complementary products (fashion, home decor) "Frequently bought together" — bundling opportunity (product page + cart) "Recently viewed" — re-engagement for browsers "Based on your history" — personalized for returning buyers "Trending in this category" — social proof for new visitors Placement Strategy Placement Show the product clearly, then help the buyer decide. Concept illustration Place recommendations at high-intent moments: below the add-to-cart button (highest converting placement), in the cart before checkout, in the post-purchase confirmation email, and on the homepage for returning visitors. Manual Override For low-volume stores or new product launches, use LetBuyy's manual "featured products" override while the AI accumulates enough data. Switch to AI mode once you have 500+ orders. L LetBuyy Team Platform 30 Apr 2026 7 min read Updated 10 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # recommendations # ai # conversion # personalization The guide, illustrated Help buyers discover products that make sense together. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 How it works 02 Types 03 Placement How Recommendations Work LetBuyy's recommendation engine uses collaborative filtering: "buyers who bought this product also bought these products." With enough order data (typically 500+ orders), the recommendations become accurate and personalized. Read this section Types of Recommendations "You may also like" — products similar to what's being viewed (product page) · "Complete the look" — complementary products (fashion, home decor) Read this section Placement Strategy Place recommendations at high-intent moments: below the add-to-cart button (highest converting placement), in the cart before checkout, in the post-purchase confirmation email, and on the homepage for returning visitors. Read this section Product recommendations drive 35% of Amazon's revenue. The same intelligence is now available to independent Indian stores through LetBuyy's recommendation engine — no ML team required. How Recommendations Work How it works Help buyers discover products that make sense together. Concept illustration LetBuyy's recommendation engine uses collaborative filtering: "buyers who bought this product also bought these products." With enough order data (typically 500+ orders), the recommendations become accurate and personalized. Types of Recommendations "You may also like" — products similar to what's being viewed (product page) "Complete the look" — complementary products (fashion, home decor) "Frequently bought together" — bundling opportunity (product page + cart) "Recently viewed" — re-engagement for browsers "Based on your history" — personalized for returning buyers "Trending in this category" — social proof for new visitors Placement Strategy Placement Show the product clearly, then help the buyer decide. Concept illustration Place recommendations at high-intent moments: below the add-to-cart button (highest converting placement), in the cart before checkout, in the post-purchase confirmation email, and on the homepage for returning visitors. Manual Override For low-volume stores or new product launches, use LetBuyy's manual "featured products" override while the AI accumulates enough data. Switch to AI mode once you have 500+ orders. L LetBuyy Team Platform 8 May 2026 8 min read Updated 13 Jun 2026 Copy link Save # automation # workflows # operations # efficiency The guide, illustrated Follow a workflow from its trigger through a decision to an action. Concept illustration Explore an idea, then read the detail. 01 Workflow ideas 02 Build a workflow The 10 Workflows Every Store Needs Order confirmed → WhatsApp confirmation + GST invoice email · Payment failed → WhatsApp retry link within 15 minutes Read this section Building Workflows in LetBuyy In your Merchant Control Plane, navigate to Automation → Workflows. Select a trigger event, define conditions (optional), and add one or more actions. Workflows run server-side — no browser tab required. Read this section A workflow is a chain of: trigger → condition → action. "When an order is placed (trigger) AND payment is confirmed (condition) → send WhatsApp confirmation + print label (action)." Build enough workflows and your store runs itself. The 10 Workflows Every Store Needs Workflow ideas Follow a workflow from its trigger through a decision to an action. Concept illustration Order confirmed → WhatsApp confirmation + GST invoice email Payment failed → WhatsApp retry link within 15 minutes Order shipped → WhatsApp with AWB link Out for delivery → WhatsApp "Your order arrives today" Delivered → Review request WhatsApp after 5 days COD order → Pre-delivery confirmation WhatsApp (reduces RTO) Stock below reorder point → Slack/email alert to operations Customer inactive 90+ days → Re-engagement WhatsApp Cart abandoned 2 hours → WhatsApp recovery message Return requested → Auto-approval for orders under ₹500 Building Workflows in LetBuyy Build a workflow Connect requests, events and access to the work your store needs. Concept illustration In your Merchant Control Plane, navigate to Automation → Workflows. Select a trigger event, define conditions (optional), and add one or more actions. Workflows run server-side — no browser tab required. Test Before Activating Always test workflows on a real ₹1 test order before activating them for all orders. A misconfigured WhatsApp workflow that sends 500 messages to the wrong number is recoverable but embarrassing.
